title: E9.T4: diagnostics that do not invent a call
description:
The reports and the ledger already know things they do not say, and there are
problems for which no repair call exists. Both halves are handled here, and the
second half is handled by refusing to invent.

Not exposed today: exact assertion outcome reasons, the coverage gaps themselves
and the identity of refused rows, tainted dimensions, and the channel metadata
needed to state independence honestly. `collect_coverage_gaps` is private and
only taints; `ImportRowResolution` is referenced in comments
(`event/mod.rs:182,3107`) and does not exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ledger exposes, for a status: why each claim outcome came out as it did,
  which dimensions are tainted and by which gap, and the channel identity that
  bears on independence.
- The flow report's unexplained residual and undecomposed rows say what is known
  about them, by account and interval.
- Where no call resolves the problem, the item is `informational` or
  `blocked_external` with `operation: null` and a stated reason. This covers, for
  now: repairing a coverage gap (no repair transition exists), obtaining
  independent confirmation (independence cannot be bound before the artefact is
  received), resolving undecomposed rows (row identities are not exposed),
  resolving a possible duplicate (no owner decision endpoint), and fixing a
  discrepancy (nothing identifies which side is wrong).
- No item invents an address. A URL that might help is not an action.
- The gap-repair half stays blocked on E4 (iaam-evc2) and says so.
close_reason: Diagnostics take the whole ledger, not its statuses: a gap can be stored with no status at all, and a signature over statuses would have compiled, passed and missed it. Six items, every one blocked with no operation and no scope. The coverage gap's category is computed, proved by mutation. Evidence renders the document rather than the source, because that is what the independence rule compares. make check: 1822 tests run, 1822 passed.

title: E9.T3: journal milestones become detectable
description:
The setup frontier ends where the journal begins. To go further the queue needs
state summaries that do not exist: whether an account holds any business fact,
the date bounds of what it holds, and whether an exact control assertion exists
for a given account, period, point and dimension.

These are purpose-built application-level queries. Transport must not load the
journal and reinterpret domain events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A summary answers, per account: has any non-control business fact, and the
  first and last dates of what is recorded.
- A query answers whether a control assertion exists for an exact
  account/period/point/dimension.
- Two detectors: `start_account_import` and `provide_control_assertion`.
- `provide_control_assertion` binds its subject fully — account, period, point
  and dimension — and presets every value the system already knows, so the agent
  copies nothing from an unrelated field. Only what the owner must state is left
  in `request.missing`, marked as coming from the owner's knowledge.
- The distinction between "first import observed" and "import complete" is
  explicit in the item's own words. An import is continuous and is never done;
  a milestone is not completeness.
- The completion check for `provide_control_assertion` is the existence of the
  matching assertion, and the item says plainly that this does not mean it
  matched: the outcome may still be provisional or become a discrepancy.
- `make check` green; each detector proved by a test that performs the action.
close_reason: Two SQL summaries — per-account business activity with its date bounds, and an exact assertion lookup — instead of loading the journal. Two detectors: start_account_import with no address, because importing is a document upload or a broker sync and the system cannot tell which, and provide_control_assertion presetting account, period and point while asking only for cash, which also satisfies by construction the cash-or-positions rule OpenAPI cannot express. The period is the first and last business effective date, the only bound the state justifies. Prose carries two load-bearing sentences: import is continuous and never complete, and an assertion is evidence rather than proof of a match. Coordinator scoped start_account_import's identity to its account — every such item shared one id, so the second was invisible to a deduplicating agent — and proved the test for it fails without the fix. make check green at 1797 tests.

title: E9.T2: GET /v1/actions, and the action contract
description:
The spine, and the home of the action contract — which lives here rather than in
T1 because this is the first task with an operation to address. A resolver
shipped without one produces a contract suite that is green and proves nothing.

Named `/v1/actions`, not `/v1/next`: "next" promises a single global sequence,
and the domain has none. What it returns is the current frontier.

The honest name for the mechanism is a **versioned action policy**, not a derived
workflow. A dependency graph would not remove hand-written knowledge; it would
relocate it into predicates, effects and ranking. A serialised requires/provides
DSL is refused outright: it needs an interpreter, a state vocabulary, typed
joins, cycle handling, evaluation errors, cost control and schema evolution — a
second framework inside the first. Detectors are typed Rust functions reading
application-level views.

What makes this better than the document it replaces is not that nothing is
written by hand. It is that the predicate runs against live state, the address
comes from a registered route, the SAME predicate is the completion check, and a
test performs the action and proves the predicate goes quiet. That is drift a
contract test catches — not immunity from drift.

A requirement is not one kind of thing, and conflating them either blocks lawful
behaviour or presents advice as obligation. Classify explicitly: `blocking`,
`required_for_goal`, `recommended`, `external_input`.

Blocked by a missing capability: there is no `list_contours`. The store loads a
contour only by known id (`ports.rs:203`), so "accounts exist, no contour" is not
computable today.

## The action contract, moved here from T1

Field names come from Arazzo 1.1.0 (OpenAPI Initiative, ratified 2026-05-17)
wherever it has one, so that this answer reads as something already known and so
that an Arazzo document could be generated from it later. We do NOT author an
Arazzo file: a hand-written workflow document drifts exactly as the skill we are
deleting. We compute; it describes.

- One envelope: `id` (stable identity for dedup, rendering and tracking across
  refreshes), `kind`, `state`, `reason`, `required_scope`, `operation`,
  `request` (`preset` / `missing`), `successCriteria`. No `executor` — no
  response assigns an HTTP call to a human (ADR-0003). No untyped `subject`: a
  tagged subject type arrives with the first real subject, which is here.
- Borrowed names, with their sources:
  - `operationId` / `operationPath` — Arazzo Step Object. `operationPath` is a
    JSON Pointer into the OpenAPI document, which is what "resolved from the
    route table" means in a standard's own words.
  - `parameters[] {name, in, value}` — Arazzo Parameter Object.
  - `successCriteria[] {context, condition, type}` — Arazzo Criterion Object,
    `type` one of `simple | regex | jsonpath`. **We extend its meaning and must
    say so:** Arazzo evaluates a criterion against the response of the step just
    taken; ours asserts an invariant that will hold once an outstanding item is
    done. Same shape, different subject.
  - `dependsOn` — Arazzo, for prerequisites between items.
  - `required`, `value`, `prompt` on a missing input — HAL-FORMS property object.
  - `pointer` — JSON Pointer (RFC 6901), as RFC 9457 §3 and JSON:API both use for
    addressing a value inside a request.
  - `input_required` as a state word — MCP Tasks.
- `reason` is **prose, not a code**. The consumer is a language model, and prose
  is its highest-bandwidth channel; `kind` already carries the typed identity
  that tests, deduplication and UI grouping need, so a second taxonomy over the
  same fact would be redundant. The prose is written for an agent: state and
  consequence, no politeness, no repetition of what `subject` already carries,
  entities named by identifier as well as name. Tests assert on `kind`, never on
  the sentence.
- `provided_by` is **ours, and deliberately so**. The survey found nothing that
  expresses where a missing value must come from: the state of the art is A2A's
  binary `INPUT_REQUIRED` versus `AUTH_REQUIRED`. Nothing distinguishes "the
  owner knows this", "an external document carries it" and "the caller sent it
  wrong". The spec must record that this is an invention and why.
- `operation` is `Option`. Where no call resolves the need it is `null` and
  `state` says why. A plausible URL that does not fix the problem is worse than
  silence: the agent will follow it.
- `request.missing` entries are JSON Pointers plus `provided_by` (`owner`,
  `external_document`, `caller`). `preset` carries what the system already knows.
- Illegal combinations are unrepresentable, not merely avoided by constructors:
  an internal sum type — operation target, option target, or no target — that
  serialises into the flat DTO. A test cannot prove future constructors behave.
- `options` (non-recursive, narrower than the envelope) ships only if a detector
  here genuinely has mutually sufficient choices. It is not reserved empty.

## Addresses come from the registered routes

- `operation_id` is the only address written by hand, on the route itself.
  `utoipa-gen` 5.5.0 takes it as an `Expr` (`src/path.rs:48`), so it is a shared
  constant.
- Resolution reads the COMPLETED document returned by `split_for_parts`, not
  `ApiDoc::openapi()`: `ApiDoc` declares schemas while paths are merged by
  `OpenApiRouter`, so the latter would advertise an unmounted operation.
  Duplicate `operation_id`s must be rejected by the scan — utoipa does not
  enforce global uniqueness.
- It proves registration, method, path, declared body and security. It does NOT
  prove the middleware chain, that runtime authorization matches the declared
  security, or that the handler accepts what the schema claims. The black-box
  test is not redundant with it.

## Construction becomes fallible, in the right order

`build(state) -> (Router, OpenApi)` has no error channel (`lib.rs:107`) and
spawns the market scheduler BEFORE assembling routers (`lib.rs:110`), so a
validation failure today would follow a background side effect.

- `build` returns `Result<_, BuildError>`; call sites in `iaam-bootstrap` and the
  contract tests are updated.
- Order: assemble routers, produce the completed document, resolve and validate
  the catalog, install it, then spawn the scheduler.
- The catalog is shared, not copied: `Arc<OnceLock<ActionCatalog>>`. `ServerState`
  is cloned into middleware before the router is complete (`lib.rs:163`), and a
  bare `OnceLock` would clone an empty cell that never fills.
- Repeated `build` on clones of one state is defined explicitly: either refused
  or idempotent with an equality check. `set` failing silently is neither.
- The `Handle::try_current()` guard before spawning (`lib.rs:107-112`) survives
  the reorder, or synchronous router tests panic for want of a runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GET /v1/actions` returns a grouped, bounded queue: `as_of`, `policy_version`,
  a summary by category, groups with counts, at most a page of items, an opaque
  keyset cursor. Never one row per account x month x dimension.
- Two detectors: `create_first_account` and `create_first_contour`, the second
  requiring a new `list_contours` through store, port and application.
- Each item carries `rank_reason`; ranking is policy and is versioned. With no
  stated goal, deterministic category order beats pretending to know the one best
  action.
- Every input the referenced schema requires is either preset or listed in
  `request.missing`. Asserting only that each listed pointer exists would pass
  while an action stayed unusable.
- Every action kind that HAS an operation resolves to exactly one, its advertised
  method and path equal the resolved operation's, and a black-box request reaches
  the handler. Non-invokable items are exempt by construction, not by a skipped
  test.
- An integration test executes each action and proves the item disappears,
  through the same predicate that produced it.
- Ordering deterministic; traversal eventual rather than a frozen snapshot, and
  the contract says so. Silent omission is not acceptable.
notes:
Token cost of the capability document, raised by draft-aiendpoint-ai-discovery (not adopted, not taken): our OpenAPI document is dozens of schemas and forty-odd routes, and an agent needing one call should not pay context for all of it. That draft's answer is a hand-written 300-800 token summary, which is a second description that drifts.

Ours must be that an action item carries operationId/operationPath, so the agent resolves ONE operation rather than fetching the document. The queue must therefore never require a full-document fetch to be usable: whatever an item advertises has to be enough to make the call, or the addressing has failed and the agent falls back to reading everything.
close_reason: Three workers plus a gate fix. list_contours through store, port and adapter (the store could answer it, an API could not). A policy layer in iaam-app naming eligibility, gap and completion apart — the test proves that losing eligibility is not completion, which is the distinction the design exists for. GET /v1/actions with a tagged target, explicit operation ids on two handlers, and a catalog resolved against the COMPLETED document from split_for_parts, with four failures named apart. build returns a Result and validates before spawning the scheduler; the Handle::try_current guard survives. Coordinator rewrote the required-input test, which compared the schema against a literal and would have stayed green while the response stopped advertising a field, and proved it fails by deleting the contour's accounts. Cut from the design after review and not shipped: pagination over a computed set, as_of, summary, groups, ranking, dependsOn, subject and a serialised condition language. make check green at 1791 tests.

title: E9.T1: discovery, and an honest refusal
description:
Spec: `.internal/specs/2026-09-02-e9-t1-discovery-and-the-action-contract-design.md`

The entry point and an honest refusal — and nothing invented. A survey of
agent-facing API standards found every part of this already specified: the entry
point by RFC 9727, the relations by RFC 8631, the format by RFC 9264, the
challenge by RFC 6750. An earlier draft invented a `GET /v1` document; withdrawn,
because a bespoke entry point is one more thing an agent must be told about out
of band.

The action envelope and route resolver live in E9.T2, where an operation exists
to exercise them. Here they would produce a green, vacuous contract suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/.well-known/api-catalog` (RFC 9727) served unprotected as
  `application/linkset+json` (RFC 9264), with RFC 8631 relations: `service-desc`
  to `/v1/openapi.json`, `status` to `/v1/health`. No bespoke discovery document.
- The catalog reads no state, and its body is byte-identical across instance
  states — asserted over status, headers and raw bytes.
- Every `href` it names resolves to a route that exists.
- The OpenAPI security scheme description states where a token comes from and
  that no route issues one. That is where the credential contract lives; a prose
  endpoint would be SKILL.md in JSON.
- `401` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` with nothing presented, and
  `Bearer error="invalid_token"` (RFC 6750 §3) when a token was rejected, plus
  `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Vary: Authorization`.
- Both refusal paths tested: a missing header returns before the rate limiter
  (`auth.rs:47-49`), a present token passes through it first (`auth.rs:50-70`).
- The missing-header body is a static serialized constant: that path is
  unlimited, so its cost is an attacker's lever.
- `POST /v1/claim` absent from router and document.
close_reason: /.well-known/api-catalog (RFC 9727) in linkset+json with service-desc and status, built from constants so it is identical across instance states rather than filtered to look that way; the test follows every href it publishes. Mounted through OpenApiRouter, so unlike /v1/openapi.json it appears in the document it points at. 401 carries a bare Bearer challenge where nothing was presented and error=invalid_token where a token was refused, with no-store and Vary on both, and a static body because that path returns before the rate limiter. The credential contract lives in the security scheme description. Coordinator replaced the worker's unauthorized(bool) with two named constructors. 100 contract tests.

title: E9 · The API's answers direct the agent, so no skill has to
description:
A skill that narrates our own API drifts from it silently. A response cannot.
`docs/agent-skill/SKILL.md` states in four places (lines 47, 82, 256, 294) that
routes answer `501` whose handlers are implemented. That is the whole argument,
already paid for.

The first design of this epic was to attach an address to every state that needs
a next step. An adversarial review and a check against the code overturned it:

- Four of the ten verdicts are never constructed by production —
  `NeedsReconciliation`, `NeedsClassification`, `Discrepancy` and `Accepted`
  appear only as match arms (`scenarios/sync.rs:512-520`). Half the acceptance
  criteria described responses that cannot occur.
- `Provisional` carries an event id and nothing else — no account, period,
  dimension or channel — so it cannot honestly say what would settle it.
  Independence is `parser_version != AND document !=`
  (`reconciliation/evidence.rs:58`), so "import another source" would be a lie.
- `ReconciliationLedger` exposes statuses only. Coverage gaps and refused rows
  are consumed, never surfaced, and no `ImportRowResolution` exists — so a
  repair action would be an invented URL.

What CAN be computed today is what the system lacks. That inverts the epic: the
state-derived work queue becomes the spine, and per-response actions become its
second carrier.

Authority is settled by ADR-0003: the owner's only surface is the agent, every
call is made by the agent, and a CLI keeps the secrets. No response ever tells a
human to make an HTTP request.

## Success Criteria

- An agent connecting to a fresh instance reaches a first import and a first
  report by following computed answers alone, reading nothing a human maintains.
- The order of setup is written nowhere — not in a document, not in the CLI, not
  in the coming web UI. It is computed, and every surface reads the same queue.
- What produces an item is a query against live state, and the same query is the
  check that the item is done. A test performs the action and proves the item
  goes quiet.
- Addresses are resolved from the registered routes, never written as strings.
- Where no call resolves a problem, the item says so and carries no address. A
  plausible URL that does not fix the problem is worse than silence: the agent
  will follow it.
design:
WHAT SHIPPED. Rewritten at close to match the code, not the plan.

The argument was already paid for: docs/agent-skill/SKILL.md told agents in four
places that implemented routes answered 501. Closing that turned out to be worse
than described — nothing in this codebase has EVER returned 501, and the same
document's verdict table listed eight codes of ten while omitting
possible_duplicate and quarantined, which production does emit. Both are fixed,
and scripts/check-agent-skill.sh now refuses a route path, an HTTP method or a
status code anywhere in that document, so it cannot make an availability claim
again. The guard checks shapes and needs no list of routes, so it cannot itself
go stale.

The spine is the computed queue. GET /v1/actions answers from store views and
never folds the journal; T3 added the journal milestones as SQL aggregates for
that reason. T4 added the diagnostics — six items, every one blocked with no
operation and no scope, because no call in this API resolves them. T5 gave them
their carrier.

FOUR THINGS THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION GOT WRONG, corrected by the work:

1. It said coverage gaps and refused rows are never surfaced, implying row
   identity was unavailable. Schema 8 added ImportCoverageGap.rows, so refused
   rows CAN be named. It is UNDECOMPOSED rows in the flow report that cannot.
2. It treated the ledger's statuses as the place diagnostics would live. A gap
   can be stored with no status at all: sync writes the gap, then returns early
   on an out-of-interval trade or a portfolio describing another day. A detector
   over statuses would have compiled, passed and missed exactly that case.
3. Independence is parser AND document — the description had this right, and an
   intermediate design still proposed exposing the SOURCE identifier, which is
   the one coordinate the rule deliberately ignores.
4. Diagnostics were assumed to be reachable from /v1/actions. They are not, and
   wiring them in is refused rather than deferred: it would fold the journal and
   the flow report on every call. A diagnostic has exactly one carrier — the
   response that computed it. 'Two carriers, one truth' is true of the ENVELOPE.

SUCCESS CRITERIA, HONESTLY SCORED:

- Order of setup computed, one queue every surface reads: MET.
- The producing query is also the completion check: MET, with the distinction
  T2 forced — eligibility, gap and completion are three predicates, not one.
- Addresses resolved from registered routes, never written as strings: MET.
- No item invents an address: MET, and guarded by an exact-set assertion.
- 'An agent reaches a first import by computed answers alone': NOT MET, and the
  reason is deliberate. start_account_import carries no operation, because the
  system cannot tell whether an import is a document upload or a broker sync.
  The agent must choose from the contract. Naming one would have been a guess
  presented as an instruction.

ADR-0003 settled authority: no response assigns an HTTP call to a human, and no
credential except its own token reaches the agent. Its consequences shipped
alongside — POST /v1/claim and the one-time code are gone, credential submission
left HTTP, and the CLI became real subcommands.

FILED, NOT FIXED: iaam-hj1o (the upload path writes no coverage gap at all,
so an upload that refused rows taints nothing), iaam-g5xk, iaam-zhvh, iaam-647w.
close_reason: All five tasks closed. make check: 1831 tests, 1831 passed. The description was rewritten at close to record what shipped, the four things the original plan got wrong, and the one success criterion deliberately not met: an agent still cannot reach a first import by computed answers alone, because the system cannot tell a document upload from a broker sync and naming one would be a guess presented as an instruction.

title: E8 · The owner's data cannot be committed, and a guard proves it
description:
A rule in CLAUDE.md is advice. It was written and broken twice in the same
session, and the second breach reached a public repository: the owner's total
capital, his month's income and expenses, and a merchant he pays were published
and had to be removed by rewriting 630 commits and recreating the repository.

What works is what the repository already does elsewhere — a guard that fails
the build. `scripts/check-architecture.sh` and `scripts/check-fixtures.sh` are
the precedent.

## The design this epic was opened with, and why it was abandoned

The original criteria asked for a guard that matches MARKERS built from the
owner's own files, kept outside the repository and named by an environment
variable, reporting partial coverage when none was configured.

Building that guard required the agent to hold his statements, and then to
assemble an allow-list of which of his words were "not really his" — from the
same files. The guard had become the leak it existed to prevent. The marker
list is gone. What replaced it is stronger and needs no configuration: the
owner's data never reaches this side at all. He runs the import skills himself;
the agent writes the tools and reads only what he chooses to paste.

## Success Criteria (as delivered)

- The guard checks SHAPES, never values. It holds no list of anybody's
  accounts, merchants or amounts, needs no configuration, and therefore runs
  identically for anyone who clones the repository.
- No data file (`.csv`, `.db`, `.xlsx`, `.pdf`, …) outside the synthetic-fixture
  directories, where `check-fixtures.sh` already freezes what lives there.
- No statement-shaped amount — groups of three, decimal comma — in a line a
  change ADDS. Checked against a base revision, because the existing tree is
  vetted and old plans legitimately carry invented amounts in that shape.
- `make check` runs it as `make privacy`, and `make hooks` installs the same
  check as `pre-commit`: a value refused before it enters a commit costs a
  keystroke, one caught afterwards costs a history rewrite.
- The guard has tests of its own: it runs its own probes on every invocation
  and fails if either rule misclassifies them. A guard nobody has seen fail is
  the advice it replaces.
- CLAUDE.md states the rule the guard cannot check — that the agent does not
  hold the operator's data at all — and names the guard as the part a rule
  cannot enforce.
close_reason: Delivered by 1c9332e and d6f5896 as a shape guard, not a marker guard. scripts/check-no-personal-data.sh refuses a data file outside the synthetic-fixture directories and a statement-shaped amount on an added line, carries its own probes, runs as make privacy inside make check, and installs as pre-commit via make hooks. The marker-list half of the original design was abandoned: building it required holding the owner's statements and then an allow-list of which of his words were not his, which made the guard the leak. The description now records that reversal so the list is not reintroduced.

title: E7.T6: balances stated, the report read, the discrepancy believed
description:
Plan Task 6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A closing control balance on 2026-08-31 exists for every in-contour account whose
  balance the owner can state, including MTS, which has a balance and no operations.
- GET /v1/reports/flow for 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 returns the six quantities, the
  internal-transfer reference block and the discrepancy.
- The discrepancy is reported as found, with its account. If non-zero, that account
  is investigated — the report is not adjusted.

title: E7.T4: the T-Bank import skill, proven on a synthetic export
description:
Plan Task 4. The institution's knowledge goes into .claude/skills/tbank-csv-import/,
never into a crate. Developed against a synthetic fixture containing none of the
owner's data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The synthetic export produces exactly the counts in fixtures/expected-summary.json
  on --dry-run, and `unaccounted` is 0.
- A transfer pair between two in-contour accounts becomes ONE transfer operation.
  Legs are matched by equal absolute amount and nearest time within 5 seconds — the
  legs differ by about a second, and exact-timestamp matching finds 1 pair of 53.
- A pair whose counterparty is outside the contour yields one withdrawal or deposit
  on the in-contour side; the outside leg is not submitted.
- An unmatched leg is reported, never guessed at.
- idempotency_key follows spec §3 exactly, including the account and channel prefix.

title: E6.T10: money is summed in the core, and versions are allocated by the store
description:
Found by the epic's architecture guard (`scripts/check-architecture.sh`), which
says plainly: "monetary arithmetic in the shell — every number in the response
must come from core (§3.1, §13). Fix the code, not the guard."

Two defects, one surfaced by the guard and one found beside it.

1. `crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/categories.rs` sums `Money` in the app layer
   (`checked_negate`, `try_add`) while building the rule preview. That
   arithmetic belongs in `iaam-core`, where the overflow discipline and the f64
   ban are tested.

2. `crates/iaam-server/src/routes.rs:667` computes the next rule version as
   `max + 1` in the HTTP handler. That is not money, but it is a race: two
   concurrent requests read the same maximum and both write version N+1, and the
   uniqueness index then rejects one of them for a reason the caller cannot act
   on. `insert_category_rule` already allocates the version atomically under an
   immediate transaction — the route must not duplicate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The preview's per-month, per-category money summation lives in `iaam-core`;
  the app scenario supplies the rows and formats the result.
- `scripts/check-architecture.sh` passes without changes to the script.
- The route no longer computes a version; the version comes back from the store
  that allocated it.
- A test proves the preview still reports the same months, amounts and counts as
  before this change.

each take seven arguments, over clippy's limit of six, and `-D warnings` makes
that an error.

The fix is a parameter object, not an `#[allow]`. `matcher_json`, `category`,
`valid_from` and `valid_to` describe one thing — the rule being written — and
passing them as four positional arguments is also how a caller silently swaps
`valid_from` and `valid_to`, which the type system currently cannot catch
because both are `Option<Date>`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `NewCategoryRule` value carries the matcher, the category and the interval;
  the three functions take it instead of four positional arguments.
- `owner` and `replaces` stay separate arguments: they are not properties of the
  rule's content.
- Every call site is updated: `crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/sqlite.rs` and
  `crates/iaam-store/tests/categories.rs`.
- `cargo clippy -p iaam-store --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- The existing category tests still pass unchanged in behaviour.

title: E5.T8: a tax can be submitted over HTTP
description:

a separate enum from `iaam_ingest::OperationKind`, so adding `OperationKind::Tax`
did not make a tax submittable through the API. The compiler cannot report this
— the two enums are converted by hand — and without it the report's tax line
stays empty forever, which is the exact defect the tax fact exists to fix.

Correction after the T8 worker pushed back: `POST /v1/ingest/operations` returns
**200 with a per-row verdict** by design (§10.1, epic iaam-40vm) — one unreadable
row must not reject the others. An earlier version of these criteria demanded 422
and contradicted that. The misleading test name
`an_invalid_amount_is_reported_as_422_with_field_expected_actual` (contract.rs)
asserts 200 and is what led there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `OperationKindDto` gains a tax variant carrying an amount magnitude, a
  currency and an origin (`withheld_at_source` / `self_paid`).
- `to_domain` maps it to `iaam_ingest::OperationKind::Tax`.
- A contract test submits a tax through `POST /v1/ingest/operations` and proves
  the stored event has one tax leg with the negated amount — asserting on the
  written event, not only on the HTTP status.
- A submitted tax of zero or a negative amount comes back as
  `verdict: "rejected"` with `field: "amount"` inside a 200 response, matching
  how fee and withdrawal already behave.
- The misleading test name above is corrected to say what it asserts.

title: E4.T1: SourceRowKey, and the coverage gap carries its rows
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-09-01-e4-coverage-gap-rows.md Task 1
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-09-01-e4-coverage-gap-names-its-rows-design.md

notes:
ACCEPTED 2026-09-01. Merged to main as b162748 (worker commit 7184910 + coordinator fix 84e7012).

Delivered: source_row.rs with SourceRowKey/RowName/RefusedRow; ImportCoverageGap gains rows; schema-aware validate_import_coverage_gap; SCHEMA_VERSION 7 to 8; the write gate in scenarios/ingest.rs refusing a mismatched schema_version; the reconciliation_ledger.rs helper synthesises rows so no existing assertion changed.

Verification: 34 test targets across iaam-core and iaam-app, zero failures.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND ON REVIEW, both caused by the brief, not the worker:

1. crates/iaam-app/tests/sync.rs did not compile: an exhaustive struct pattern missing the new field. The brief prescribed cargo check -p, which does not build test targets, so the worker could not have caught it. LESSON: any task widening an EventKind variant must also run cargo test -p for every crate with integration tests over that variant.

2. Regression: the producer stamped schema_version 8 with an empty row list, and schema-8 validation refuses that, so sync_broker could no longer record a coverage gap. Nine tests failed. Root cause was the plan, which told Task 1 to leave rows empty until Task 4. The type change and the producer change cannot land separately.

Both fixed by the coordinator in 84e7012, which also folded in the producer half originally scoped as Task 4a.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: Task 4 now covers only the resolution-appending half, which still depends on Task 2. The row-filling half is done. Task 3 (row-aware idempotency key, iaam-lg4q) is untouched and still required.
