title: [bug] collect_groups reads the raw journal, so a reversed control assertion still produces evidence
notes:
Severity: Important
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-core/src/reconciliation/mod.rs:220-222 — build_with computes
'let effective_events = resolve(events)?' and then calls collect_groups(events) and
collect_coverage_gaps(events) on the RAW slice. resolve() correctly drops both a
reversed target and the reversal event itself (crates/iaam-core/src/event/correction.rs).

Consequence: a control assertion that was reversed still forms a StatementGroup, is
still checked against the projection, and can still raise a dimension's status through
grounds 1, 2, 3 and 5. Retracting a wrong assertion therefore does not withdraw the
confirmation it produced — a false confirmation.

The effective_events value IS used, but only for observe() inside the loop, so the
projection is correct while the evidence built on top of it is not.

Same class as iaam-serr, which corrected the sync refusal predicate to read the
effective set. Found by an adversarial codex review of the E4 design; the coverage-gap
half of the same defect is inside epic iaam-evc2, this half is independent of it.
close_reason: collect_groups and collect_coverage_gaps take &[&Event] and receive resolve()'s effective set, as observe() already did. A reversed control assertion no longer forms a group — it formed one twice, since a reversal carries the kind of its target — and a reversed coverage gap no longer taints. Same class as iaam-serr; iaam-tyvi had scoped these two out on the ground that a TRADE reversal cannot reach them, which holds and is not the case that broke. 2 tests, red first. E4's design section 7 updated: only the resolution collector remains.

title: The coverage gap's idempotency key ignores which rows were refused, so a new missing row is suppressed by an old repaired gap
description:
Severity: Important
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/sync.rs:365 builds the gap identity from
(account, from, to, source, parser_version, dimensions, refused) — the union of
dimensions and the COUNT of refused rows, never the rows themselves. That string
becomes the idempotency key (:392), and a colliding gap is then skipped as a duplicate.

Consequence, and it is a false confirmation rather than a false taint: refuse row A
affecting {Cash}, count 1; repair it; a later import refuses a DIFFERENT row B, also
{Cash}, also count 1. The new gap collides with A's key and is never appended. The
journal then holds only the gap for A, and any rule that lifts a gap once its row is
present treats the interval as clean while B is still missing.

Today this is latent: the current correlation never lifts a gap at all, so the missing
second gap changes nothing observable. It goes live the moment a gap can be repaired,
which is what epic iaam-evc2 is for. Filed separately because it is a defect in the
key, not in the correlation rule, and it survives any choice of recovery model.

Found by an adversarial codex review of the E4 design, verified against the tree.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Refuse a row affecting {Cash}; a gap is recorded with `refused: 1`.
2. Repair that row.
3. Refuse a different row, also affecting {Cash}, also one row.
4. The second gap collides with the first one's idempotency key and is skipped as a duplicate: the journal holds only the first gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- The coverage gap's identity distinguishes which rows were refused, not merely how many. Refusing row A, repairing it, then refusing a different row B in the same dimension records two gaps, not one.
- Proven by a test that refuses A, repairs it, refuses B, and asserts both gaps are in the journal.
- Independent of the recovery model: the key is fixed here whichever way iaam-evc2 decides correlation.

title: T-Invest: a per-row refusal is not a response-wide verdict
notes:
Three defects share one shape: something true of one row, or of one import attempt, is applied to the whole response or the whole interval.

Ordered so each can be designed, reviewed and shipped on its own, and so that no task makes an unfixed neighbour fire more often:

T1 iaam-9zur - the portfolio must not be recorded as the closing balance of an interval it does not describe. A precondition: T3's answer is 'record the assertions instead of suppressing them', which makes this defect fire more often rather than less.
T2 iaam-bl07 - a per-row refusal is quarantined and the batch continues, at both the adapter layer and the normalisation layer (sync.rs:118). A defect of our own code must still abort loudly.
T3 iaam-dbvu - a quarantined row disqualifies its own import attempt from granting independent evidence, per dimension, instead of suppressing every assertion of the interval.

The design was reviewed adversarially by codex before any task was written, and the review overturned the first answer: an interval-wide confidence cap is bypassable (raise() is monotonic max at reconciliation/mod.rs:614, and both merge_status and with_external_evidence apply later), has no recovery semantics in an append-only journal, and asserts something false - a rejected row does not prove the journal is incomplete, since the same operation may already be present from a report. The chosen mechanism disqualifies the attempt, not the interval.

Discovered-from: brainstorming session iaam-vsrx.

Known weaknesses deliberately left, both pre-existing: confirmed_dimensions compares channels by Dimension only, not by currency or instrument (reconciliation/mod.rs:559-580); Dimension::TaxBasis is constrained only by TaxWithheldTotal (claim.rs:121), which T-Invest never sends.

title: [bug] The T-Invest portfolio is recorded as the closing balance of an interval it does not describe
notes:
Severity: Critical
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/tinkoff.rs:86-97 — fetch_portfolio takes 'at' as _at and discards it, calling get_portfolio, which the contract defines as the CURRENT portfolio: docs/api/tinkoff-invest/operations.proto:96-104, PortfolioRequest carries account_id and an optional display currency and no date at all. crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/sync.rs:168-184 then records those claims through assertion_event with AssertionTarget { from, to }, dated CashPostedDate(to) and EffectiveOrder::new(to, order) (sync.rs:313-346).

So for any sync whose 'to' is not the current date, today's holdings are appended to the journal as a control assertion about a past interval. The journal is append-only: a false ControlAssertion cannot be edited, only reversed. Reconciliation then compares it against the projection for that interval (crates/iaam-core/src/reconciliation/mod.rs:build_with), producing either a false Discrepant that sends the owner to investigate a difference that is an artefact of our own request, or - worse - a false Matched that raises the interval to accepted_independent on evidence about a different day.

The date is not merely unpassed: the gateway has no historical portfolio method, so the port signature promises something this channel cannot deliver. The fix is therefore a refusal or a period the channel can honour, not plumbing the argument through.

Found by codex while designing the iaam-dbvu fix, then verified against the contract. It is a precondition for iaam-dbvu: that bead's answer is 'record the assertions instead of suppressing them', which makes this defect fire more often rather than less.
close_reason:
T1 done on branch t1-portfolio-as-of, commit ccd9a2b. The port stopped promising what a channel cannot give: fetch_portfolio returns PortfolioSnapshot with PortfolioAsOf::{Requested, Current}, the adapter states its own contract without gaining a clock, and the scenario resolves it. A current portfolio dated outside the requested interval records no assertion and SyncOutcome names why (AssertionsWithheld::PortfolioDescribesAnotherDay, additive on the wire).

Rejected on the way: recording the claims over [today, today]. They would be true, but a March sync would then append an assertion about today against a journal holding nothing after March, and the resulting discrepancy would be an artefact of the request. A true statement recorded where it answers a different question is not an improvement on a false one.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t1-portfolio-as-of-design.md. Implemented by an omp worker in an isolated worktree; the coordinator restored a BrokerChannelFactory doc comment the worker had deleted, removed a stray blank line, formatted, and ran the gates the worker was not allowed to run.

Gates: cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean, clippy -p iaam-app -p iaam-server --all-targets clean, cargo fmt clean, nextest -p iaam-app -p iaam-server 244/244 (was 236).

title: T7: the channel's money arithmetic lives in the shell
description:
Found by the epic's end-of-epic gate, not by any task's own gate: scripts/check-architecture.sh guard 9 refuses monetary arithmetic in crates/iaam-app/src and crates/iaam-server/src, because 'every number in an API response comes from core' (3.1, 13). iaam-ingest is excluded on purpose - it collects a fact from source fields rather than calculating a result.

T2 and T3 put the channel's arithmetic in crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/tinkoff.rs: summing trade quantities, the per-fill product quantity x price, the order completeness comparison, and the largest-remainder allocation of commission and accrued interest. Eleven hits.

The guard is textual - it greps for .checked_add/.checked_sub/.checked_mul/.try_add/.try_sub/.checked_negate - so calling a core primitive from the adapter still trips it, and that is the intended reading: the shell must not COMPOSE arithmetic. The whole computation has to be a named operation in iaam-core that the adapter calls once.

Nothing about the rules changes. T3's design decided them and they stay decided; this is relocation, and the operations gain their own tests in core where they belong.

This is the epic's own debt, not a follow-up: the branch does not pass make check until it is done.
close_reason:
T7 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted). Four named operations moved from crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/tinkoff.rs into iaam-core: sum_quantities and gross_for_fill into money.rs beside their siblings, check_order_completeness and the largest-remainder allocate_minor into rules/trade_allocation.rs because they encode decisions rather than representation. The adapter now calls each once and composes no arithmetic.

No rule changed. Verified by the condition set in the design: every existing test in iaam-app, iaam-broker, iaam-ingest and iaam-store passes with its expectations unmodified. The move added 11 core tests (1379 to 1390 over five crates) covering uneven allocation, fewer units than weights, a product finer than the currency's minor unit, magnitude comparison, and overflow refusal for each operation.

The allocation preserves both earlier decisions: remainders descending, ties by ascending input index, and the adapter passes weights already in emission order - (at, num) from T2 section 7 - so the tie-break is still by trade number.

Guard: grep for the six banned arithmetic methods under crates/iaam-app/src and crates/iaam-server/src returns nothing; ./scripts/check-architecture.sh passes.

Root cause worth recording: T3's design decided WHAT the arithmetic computes and never said WHERE it lives, and the worker brief pointed at the adapter. The guard is a shell script over the source tree that runs in seconds and does not compile anything, so it could have been in every task's gate; it was excluded along with the genuinely heavy workspace gates. Sequential workers make that exclusion unnecessary for the cheap guards.

title: [bug] Structural validation never runs for operations: validate_structure gates only journal facts
description:
Found while reviewing iaam-bt8r. Event::validate_structure is the input gate described in §4.3/§4.8 - the check that stops a contradictory fact entering the append-only journal, because 'the projection invariant will stop the report, but the recorded fact can only be fixed by reversal'.

Non-test callers, from grep -rn validate_structure across crates: crates/iaam-ingest/src/journal_event.rs:394 only. That is the typed corporate-action path (POST /v1/ingest/journal-events).

Operations normalised through iaam-ingest::normalize - which is every broker-channel row and every report row - never reach it. So for those channels nothing enforces that a Trade's cash leg equals gross +/- fee +/- accrued, that the security leg agrees with the declared instrument and quantity, that legs belong to the event's own account, or any of the other structural invariants. The very example the doc comment gives - an event saying 'bought one hundred units of X' whose leg credits one unit of Y to another account - would be recorded by the broker path today.

In practice the ingestion code builds legs from the same fields it declares, so the contradiction does not arise from that code. That is a property of the current implementation, not of the journal: it makes every future change to those builders unguarded, and it means the basis_fee invariant just added is dead code on the paths that actually produce trades.

Worth checking as part of the fix: whether the verdict for a structurally invalid row should be Rejected (§10.1) with the validation error as its reason, which would make the failure visible to the owner rather than silent.
close_reason: Structural validation now gates every journal write: append_checked + structural_rejection at the acceptance boundary; a structurally invalid channel row becomes Verdict::Rejected and its dimensions land in the ImportCoverageGap

title: T5: pagination, and the interval boundary it depends on
description:
The response is paginated (operations.proto:476-477) and fetch_operations reads exactly one page (adapters/tinkoff.rs, client.rs:150). parse_operations refuses only the case where hasNext is true and the cursor is missing (parse.rs:127-134); with a cursor present, later pages are lost silently while the doc comment calls the result 'a complete response'.

Following the cursor is mechanical: repeat from, to and the limit unchanged, track every cursor seen so an A-B-A cycle is caught, and make an exhausted page limit a refusal rather than a truncation.

The part that cannot be deferred - revision 3 tried - is the interval boundary. The adapter sends the final day as midnight at its start (adapters/tinkoff.rs:63) while the application interval includes the whole final day (reconciliation/claim.rs:20), and the contract calls 'to' only the end of the period. Paginating the wrong interval perfectly is still truncation, and sync_broker would then record a closing portfolio assertion over an interval missing most of the closing day. Resolve the boundary here or the pagination work claims a completeness it does not have.
close_reason:
T5 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted, on top of T1-T4). Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t5-pagination-design.md, reviewed adversarially by codex together with T6.

Pagination: parse_operations returns OperationsPage { operations, has_next, next_cursor } instead of discarding the page information behind a doc comment that called one page 'a complete response'. fetch_operations follows the cursor with from, to and limit unchanged, limit set explicitly to the contract maximum of 1000, every cursor recorded so an A-B-A cycle refuses, and a page cap of 100. A repeated cursor, an exhausted cap and the existing hasNext-without-cursor are all BrokerError, never partial operations, because the caller records a control assertion on the strength of the result.

The page cap boundary was stated two ways in the first draft and the review caught it: a response arriving as page 100 with hasNext false is COMPLETE and is accepted; only hasNext still true after page 100 refuses. The always-hasNext test cannot distinguish those, so both are tested.

Interval boundary: the request now sends the last instant of the final day rather than midnight at its start. That is safe under both readings of the contract - which never says whether to is inclusive - at the cost of one representable instant under the exclusive reading; the alternative, the start of the following day, is wrong under the inclusive reading in a worse way, because a fact would belong to two intervals.

The review found a third question that outranks both: the contract does not say WHICH timestamp from/to filter. OperationItem.date is the order date, OperationItemTrade.date is the execution date, and since T2 a fact is dated from the latter. T5 does not guess: establishing it is filed as iaam-gawg, and the discrepancy is made visible from our own data - if any fact of this sync carries a trade date outside the interval, the facts are recorded and the control assertion is suppressed, on the same path a quarantined row already takes.

Coordinator finding: the page loop ended in unreachable! kept plausible by a duplicated in-loop cap check. Fixed structurally, as in T1 - the loop no longer tracks the page number and the cap error is returned after it.

Gates run by the coordinator in the worktree: cargo check -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app --all-targets clean, nextest -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app -p iaam-ingest 311/311 (was 304).

title: T4: custody comes from position_uid, and old facts are repaired
description:
Trades fabricate custody as CustodyId(account.inner()) (adapters/tinkoff.rs:236) while portfolio claims use position_uid (parse.rs:186-192), so positions derived from trades cannot reconcile against the broker's portfolio.

The switch itself is small. The hard half is the existing data, and revision 3 got it wrong: re-importing is NOT repair. Old facts carry the old identity and account-derived custody; new ones carry a different identity and position-derived custody, and custody is part of OperationKind so the content fingerprint differs too. The new event is therefore Fresh and is inserted BESIDE the old one, double-counting the position.

This task must produce an actual strategy - reversal, replacement, or a refusal to re-import affected history - and prove it on a seeded journal. Existing adapter tests assume the fabricated custody and must be rewritten around the real identifier.
close_reason:
T4 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted, on top of T1-T3). Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t4-custody-design.md, reviewed adversarially by codex - four findings, three of them the design being factually wrong.

Custody now comes from the row's positionUid; a trading row without one is quarantined naming the field, with no fallback to the account. This aligns the trade side with the portfolio side, which already puts positionUid into ControlClaim::PositionQuantity.custody.

The hard half was the existing data, and the review changed the answer twice. The detection predicate is NOT the parser version: tinkoff-api/3 was bumped by T2 while the trade branches still fabricated custody, so a fact from this very branch would be /3 and defective, and a version predicate would bless it. It is also not the source channel: the persisted SourceChannel carries an opaque SourceId that is the currently active broker-access record, so facts recorded through a since-revoked access would not compare equal. The predicate is the defect itself - a Trade event on the account with a security leg whose custody equals CustodyId(account.inner()).

The check reads the WHOLE history through Date::MAX, not the vector sync_broker already had: that one is bounded by the synced interval, and a narrow interval is exactly what an owner requests when re-importing a suspicious month. The dedup vector stays bounded by to. Refusal is per account, before any append, and names the count and iaam-y3a2.

Also corrected: the claim that reconciliation can never match was too strong. A claim about a zero holding matches either way because an absent custody key reads as zero, so the failure was invisible precisely where nothing is held.

Proven rather than asserted: a reconciliation test where the same claim Matches with position-derived custody and is Discrepant with account-derived custody, plus four seeded-journal sync cases including an affected trade dated outside the requested interval.

Filed: iaam-y3a2 (P2) the actual reversal-and-replacement repair, which needs a maintenance entry point that does not exist; iaam-xep0 (P3) whether this channel's custody should be a custodian rather than a position identifier.

Gates run by the coordinator in the worktree: cargo check -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app --all-targets clean, nextest -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app -p iaam-ingest 304/304 (was 296).

title: T3: money of a trade - price, commission, accrued interest
description:
The money half, deliberately separated from T2 so it can be reviewed on its own.

Settled already: the cash leg must equal what the source reported - payment is exactly quantity x price for the recorded share purchase, commission excluded - and the commission reaches the lot basis through basis_fee, never through fee (validate_trade enforces cash_leg == gross +/- fee +/- accrued, event/mod.rs:352).

Unsettled, and each one blocked revision 3:
- The money-completeness equation per family. Comparing a positive product with a negative payment needs a stated sign rule. The accrued-interest term is inferred from a fixture containing only shares with zero accrued interest; the contract's own broker-report model distinguishes order_amount 'without accrued interest', aci_value and total_order_amount (operations.proto:276), which suggests the bond case differs.
- Commission allocation across fills. Pro rata by quantity assumes a per-unit fee; a turnover-based fee would need notional. The contract does not say which. Whatever rule is chosen, the rounded parts must be proven to sum back to the rounded aggregate - independent rounding in basis_fee_money (operation.rs:513) does not guarantee it.
- Accrued interest. A known zero cannot currently be recorded: fee_money routes it through positive(), which rejects zero (operation.rs:271,500). Fixing that is part of this task. Multi-day fills cannot have a time-accrued aggregate split by quantity, and leaving it unknown makes the cash settlement disagree with the source aggregate - that consequence needs a stated policy, not silence.

Depends on T2.
close_reason:
T3 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted, on top of T1 and T2). Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t3-trade-money-design.md, reviewed adversarially by codex - five findings, two of which were the design being wrong rather than incomplete.

The three unsettled questions, as settled. Completeness: one equation per ORDER, |payment| == sum(quantity x price) + |accrued_int|, on magnitudes, with the sign checked separately against the family (Buy strictly negative, Sell strictly positive, zero refused). The accrued term is a reading supported by the broker's own trade model in the same contract file - order_amount 'Сумма без НКД', aci_value, total_order_amount 'Сумма сделки' (operations.proto:276-278) - and a mismatch quarantines rather than records a distorted fact.

Commission: allocated in minor units from the rounded aggregate, weighted by QUANTITY, largest remainder, ties by trade.num as bytes. Quantity rather than notional because crates/iaam-core/src/projection/lots.rs:381 already allocates an actual payment to lots in proportion to quantity, and with no evidence either way the existing convention wins; the turnover reading is filed as iaam-jsvd.

The invariant the bead demanded - rounded parts summing to the rounded aggregate - was first declared impossible against validate_trade's per-event rule. That was wrong: what is impossible is holding both WHILE ALSO keeping each fill's exact share proportional. Allocating in minor units gives up the sub-minor proportional share, which is not a source fact, and holds both invariants by construction. A fill allocated zero units records None in both basis-fee fields, because validate_trade refuses a zero basis_fee and refuses one field without the other.

Accrued interest: its own conversion accepting zero, separate from fee_money. An accruedInt with an empty currency is None, not a known zero - the recorded response sends exactly that shape (fixture:175-179) and parse_optional_money already maps it to None, so every recorded row yields None and the known-zero path is a capability the evidence does not exercise. A non-zero accrued interest whose fills span more than one UTC date quarantines; without accrued interest the dates are irrelevant and a two-day order produces two facts, which is the parent design's case 5.

Coordinator findings beyond the review: the multi-date quarantine was initially unconditional, which refused case 5 and led the worker to weaken an existing T2 test - restored; and the dates compared were not UTC-normalised while the recorded dates were.

Filed: iaam-9wh2 (P2) - normalize substitutes zero for an absent accrued interest in the cash leg, which is why T3 quarantines its own case rather than relying on unknown being visible. iaam-jsvd (P3) - commission weighting evidence.

Gates run by the coordinator in the worktree: cargo check -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app --all-targets clean, nextest -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app -p iaam-ingest 296/296 (three-crate baseline was 282).

title: T2: one trade becomes one fact
description:
Expand a trading row into one SubmittedOperation per element of trades_info.trades, with quantity, price and timestamp from the trade. Requires ChannelTrade { num, at: OffsetDateTime, quantity, price } and the currently discarded quantity_done, quantity_rest, cancel_reason.

Blocking questions this task must settle, all raised by review and none yet answered:
- Identity. {operation_id}#{num} does not prevent a collision when one order repeats a num, which the contract nowhere forbids (operations.proto:522 says only 'Номер сделки'). Either establish uniqueness or refuse an order containing duplicate nums. The joining format must be injective: percent-escaping must escape % itself, fix one byte encoding, and be tested against components containing # and /.
- Ordering. Two economically identical fills at the same timestamp share a raw_hash, so compare_for_replay (event/mod.rs) falls back to insertion order and the response order still decides. The core gives stable order for unequal times or unequal content, not unconditionally.
- Timezone. ChannelTrade.at is an OffsetDateTime; the trade date and the source time must be derived in one declared zone, stated in the design.
- Completeness by quantity: sum of trades quantity against quantity_done, which is a proto3 scalar where absent and zero are indistinguishable.

Depends on T1 for the state contract.
close_reason:
T2 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted, on top of T1). One trading row expands into one SubmittedOperation per element of trades_info.trades; quantity, price and moment come from the trade. Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t2-trade-becomes-fact-design.md, reviewed adversarially by codex (three findings, all folded in).

The four blocking questions the bead named, as settled: identity is the percent-escaped {op}#{num} composite with % escaped first, and a duplicate num within one order quarantines the row rather than being resolved by array position; ordering is handled by emitting fills sorted by (at, num), because identical fills are NOT interchangeable - lot ids follow replay order and a later disposal reports which lot it consumed, so the audit trail would otherwise depend on gateway response order; the zone is UTC, with the 00:00-03:00 MSK failure mode stated and filed as iaam-m7hy; quantity_done is present-with-value-zero.

Two findings the review produced beyond the bead: the trade price is CalcMoney, not ChannelMoney, because parse_money refuses a fraction finer than the currency's minor units while the contract puts no such limit on a trade price; and the per-fill gross is the exact product rounded once through CalcMoney::rounded_minor, as a positive magnitude.

One coordinator finding: the first implementation gated trade parsing on the literals OPERATION_TYPE_BUY/SELL in the parser, which contradicts operation_kind.rs:9-14 - the code-to-meaning mapping lives in the dictionary, in data. Replaced by a shape rule: a trade element with an empty price currency is a placeholder and yields no ChannelTrade for any family. Expansion stays keyed on the dictionary-resolved kind in the adapter.

TINKOFF_PARSER_VERSION is tinkoff-api/3; it stays /3 for the rest of the epic provided the epic lands as one branch. Gates run by the coordinator in the worktree: cargo check -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app --all-targets clean, nextest 158/158 (was 144).

title: T1: order state becomes a typed contract
description:
ChannelOperation.state is parsed as a String and read by nobody (parse.rs:93; grep for '.state' outside parse.rs finds only unrelated types). Make it a typed enum with an Unrecognised(String) variant carrying the raw text, and gate EVERY operation family on it, not only trades - revision 2 of the spec gated only Buy/Sell, leaving coupons and fees unguarded.

Open question this task must answer rather than assume: what a non-Executed state MEANS for a family that has no independent execution evidence. A cancelled coupon is not a cancelled trade: a trade can be checked against trades_info, a coupon cannot. Define the behaviour per state per family, and say which cases are refused for lack of evidence.

No money, no dates, no expansion into several facts. Those are T2 and T3.

Contract: OPERATION_STATE_EXECUTED is 'Исполнена частично или полностью' (operations.proto:296), so this task must not treat EXECUTED as proof of completeness.
close_reason: T1 done in worktree t1-order-state (uncommitted). ChannelOrderState is a typed enum with Unrecognised(String); the state gate runs in adapt_operations after dictionary.kind_of and before operation_to_submitted, so every family is gated, not only Buy/Sell. Only Executed produces a fact; every other state produces one quarantine row, per-row, not aborting the batch. Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t1-order-state-design.md, reviewed adversarially by codex (four findings, all folded in). Gates run by the coordinator in the worktree: cargo check -p iaam-broker -p iaam-app --all-targets clean, nextest 144/144 (was 135). Known and deliberate: the executed trade path still takes quantity from the order, so iaam-d8b.23's partial-fill overstatement stands until T2 (design 3.7); the transitional quarantine for cancelled and in-progress trades is T2's to remove.

title: [epic] T-Invest: a trade becomes a fact
description:
Replaces the monolithic design in .internal/specs/2026-08-31-tinkoff-execution-facts-design.md, which failed three adversarial reviews. The failures were structural: one document covering order state, dates, quantities, commission, accrued interest, custody, pagination, securities transfers, identity and ordering has too many couplings to verify at once. The same happened before epic iaam-jdmc, and splitting fixed it.

Children are ordered so each can be designed, reviewed and shipped on its own. The spec stays as the record of what was learned; each child gets its own small design.

Preconditions already delivered by iaam-jdmc: account-scoped identity, PossibleDuplicate reaching the owner, source-derived intraday order, and a basis-only trade fee.

Parent bug: iaam-d8b.23, which stays open until every child is closed.
close_reason:
All seven children closed. Work is in worktree /home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/iaam/t1-order-state, branch t1-order-state, UNCOMMITTED. Workspace gates green: make check exit 0, 1633 tests, architecture guards passed, diff-lint passed against origin/main.

T1 typed the order state and gated every family on it. T2 expanded a trading row into one fact per fill with a declared emission order. T3 settled the money: order-level completeness with a stated sign rule, commission allocated in minor units by quantity with largest remainder, accrued interest distinguishing a known zero from an unreported one. T4 took custody from position_uid and refuses to sync an account holding facts with account-derived custody rather than doubling its position. T5 followed the cursor and fixed the interval boundary. T6 stopped recording securities transfers as cash. T7 moved the arithmetic into the core after the architecture guard refused it in the shell.

PARSER VERSION AND RE-IMPORT, the criterion the parent design required this reason to carry: TINKOFF_PARSER_VERSION is tinkoff-api/3, bumped once by T2 and unchanged by T3 to T7, on the stated condition that the epic lands as ONE branch with no release between its tasks. If it is split, each task that changes fact construction must bump again.

Facts recorded under tinkoff-api/1 and /2 carry account-derived custody and ordered rather than executed quantities. They are NOT repaired by this epic. Re-importing them is not repair: the re-imported fact differs in custody and identity, so dedup returns Fresh and the position doubles. T4 therefore refuses to sync an affected account at all until iaam-y3a2 exists, which means an owner with such history cannot sync that account. That is deliberate and is the price of not doubling silently.

Ten beads were filed along the way rather than folded in: iaam-bl07, iaam-9wh2, iaam-y3a2, iaam-2y5k, iaam-gawg, iaam-jsvd, iaam-m7hy, iaam-8j6h, iaam-xep0, iaam-8d7g. Four are defects found while designing; the rest need live gateway evidence or an owner's decision.

Every design was reviewed adversarially by codex; five reviews, sixteen findings, all folded in. Six of those findings were a design being factually wrong about the code rather than merely incomplete.

title: [bug] basis_fee has no event invariant: validate_trade never sees it
description:
Introduced by iaam-7xe8 (C4) and found in the third adversarial review of the T-Invest spec.

EventKind::Trade carries basis_fee and basis_fee_exact (kind.rs:141-146), but the dispatcher in Event::validate_structure destructures Trade with '..' (event/mod.rs:230-240), so neither field reaches validate_trade. Nothing checks that basis_fee is positive, that its currency matches the trade's, or that it agrees with basis_fee_exact.

The adapter path happens to impose some of this - basis_fee_money takes the magnitude and checks currency (operation.rs:513-535) - but that is a property of one ingestion path, not of the fact. Any other producer, a hand-built journal event, or a deserialised payload can carry a negative or foreign-currency basis fee into the append-only journal, where lots.rs:778 will add it to the lot basis.

This is the same class of defect the trade invariant already guards against for gross/fee/accrued: validate_trade exists because 'an event saying bought one hundred units of X whose leg credits one unit of Y passes validation and enters the journal forever'.

Fix: destructure both fields and validate them - positive magnitude, currency equal to the trade's, and the rounded value consistent with the exact one. Add the negative tests alongside the existing trade-validation ones.
close_reason:
Implemented by an omp worker and accepted on the diff. validate_trade now receives basis_fee and basis_fee_exact (the dispatcher no longer swallows them behind '..') and enforces four things: the posted fee is a positive magnitude, both fields carry the trade's currency, they are present or absent together, and the exact value rounds to the posted one. trade_settlement still ignores both, which is the point of the field.

One correction I found while reviewing, and it mattered: ingestion took the magnitude for the posted basis fee but stored basis_fee_exact as the raw source value, which for T-Invest is negative. The new invariant would then have failed every real purchase (-14 against +14) the moment anything validated the event. Fixed at the same place the posted value takes its magnitude; the test feeds -0.135065, expects +0.135065, and calls validate_structure so the invariant is exercised rather than assumed.

Verified by the coordinator: architecture guard passes, 93 selected tests across four packages pass.

Separate finding, filed as its own bead: validate_structure appears to be reached only from the journal-fact path (journal_event.rs:394) and never for operations normalised through normalize(), so this invariant - and every other structural one - does not currently gate the broker and report channels at all.

title: C4: a fee is exact and still equals its cash leg
description: Money is minor-unit i64 (money.rs:60), event/mod.rs:352 requires the cash leg to equal trade_settlement(gross, fee, accrued) exactly, and parse.rs:350 refuses a nano amount that is not representable. T-Invest withholds at nano precision, so a purchase is refused in full today (tinkoff_mapping.rs:45-52, adapters/tinkoff.rs:526-546). PerUnitAmount (money.rs:326) holds finer-than-minor-unit values but is a calculated per-security value with no path back to Money. Needs a decision on where rounding happens and how the exact amount and its rounding evidence are retained — which likely moves SCHEMA_VERSION. Acceptance: a nano-precision commission reaches the journal without being rounded away and without breaking the cash-leg equality; the rounding, where it happens, is evidenced.
close_reason:
Implemented by an omp worker and accepted on the diff, with the scope narrowed by a codex consultation the owner asked for.

The task turned out not to be about precision. Two amounts were conflated: the commission as a component of the trade's cash movement, and the commission as a component of the lot basis. For T-Invest they are different things - the BUY row's payment is exactly -270.13 (= 1 x price), and the commission arrives as its own BROKER_FEE row.

Delivered: the operation's commission is parsed exactly as CalcMoney with no divisibility check and is field-local, so a nano-precision commission no longer rejects the whole trading row; EventKind::Trade carries basis_fee (posted, rounded) plus basis_fee_exact (the exact value, retained for audit); basis is gross + fee + basis_fee and proceeds are gross - fee - basis_fee; the T-Invest adapter sets fee_minor: None and fills the basis fee. The cash-leg invariant at event/mod.rs:352 is untouched. TINKOFF_PARSER_VERSION goes /1 to /2, because rows previously rejected are now accepted and that is what provenance.rs:32-33 says the version exists to record.

Effect that matters: the SBER purchase now reaches the journal. The adapter test that asserted accepted.len() == 2 now asserts 3.

Verified by the coordinator: architecture guard passes; 81 selected tests pass; checked the sign by hand, since a negative basis fee would have quietly LOWERED the basis - basis_fee_money takes the magnitude via abs() and rounds 13.5065 kopeks to 14, and a_basis_only_fee_increases_acquisition_basis_without_changing_cash proves basis 1_010_000 -> 1_010_014 while the cash effect stays gross + fee only.

Deliberately NOT done, and not an oversight: the fee's own cash movement is still unposted and the BROKER_FEE row still quarantined. Summing every payment in the recorded response gives 199729.734935 against the broker's reported 199729.73, which proves a settlement rule exists and does not reveal it; CalcMoney documents that a calculated value becomes posted only through a confirmed source fact, never by rounding (money.rs:254-258). Deciding it needs a live sequence with balances around one fee. Blocked on the owner, like iaam-mnz.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Codex consultation plus arithmetic on the fixture changed what this task is about. It is not primarily about precision.

Verified by computing the fixture: the BUY row's payment is exactly -270.130000000, which is 1 x the trade price 270.130000000. The commission 0.135065 is NOT part of it; it arrives as its own OPERATION_TYPE_BROKER_FEE row whose payment is -0.135065.

So putting the commission into fee_minor makes trade_settlement produce -270.27 (operation.rs:337-341) and posts a cash movement the source never reported. Codex's phrasing is right: it fabricates cash and risks counting the fee twice, since reconciliation totals every fee leg (reconciliation/observed.rs:538).

But the commission is required in the lot basis (lots.rs:774, §7.2). The two roles of EventKind::Trade.fee - a component of the cash leg AND a component of basis - are the same field, and for this channel they diverge: the money moves separately, the basis still needs the number.

That, not nano precision, is the real content of C4. Precision is a second-order problem on top of it.

Codex also established (invariants.rs:28,145) that BasisConserved only checks acquired = remaining + released and never compares basis against cash, so 'exact basis, posted cash' does not violate a present invariant. It cannot be done by adding one field though: basis, released basis, proceeds, realised result and lot_disposal.rs:218 are all minor-unit Money, and CalcMoney already exists for exactly this distinction (money.rs:249). Moving them coherently is the size of this task.

Verdict carried over: unsafe as I proposed it. Needs a source-faithful cash/fee split plus an exact basis pipeline. Do C3 first.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Decision, after a codex consultation the owner asked for and arithmetic I ran myself. The framing 'round or refuse' was wrong; the answer is to stop conflating two amounts.

Evidence against inventing a rounding rule: summing every payment in the recorded response gives 199729.734935, while the broker's own portfolio reports totalAmountCurrencies = 199729.73 (tests/fixtures/api/tinkoff-portfolio.json). So a rounding or settlement rule demonstrably exists on the broker's side - and this single sample cannot tell floor from half-up, because 0.734935 rounds down either way. Posting 0.14 would be us inventing that rule.

Evidence from our own code, which settles it: CalcMoney is documented as having deliberately NO transition back to Money, because 'a calculated value becomes a posted amount only through a confirmed source fact, not by rounding the result' (crates/iaam-core/src/money.rs:254-258). Rounding a calculated fee into a posted one is already forbidden by design, not merely by §3.4.

Codex's counterweight, which I accept: the BROKER_FEE row is labelled 'Удержание комиссии' and is EXECUTED, so calling it a pure accrual would also overstate what we know. We do not know the settlement rule in either direction.

So C4 splits, and none of the parts invents anything:

1. Make commission parsing FIELD-LOCAL. A non-representable commission must stop rejecting the whole trading row (parse.rs:309 keep_or_reject plus parse.rs:350). The purchase then reaches the journal, which today it does not at all.
2. Keep the exact 0.135065 as source evidence of CalcMoney grade, feeding basis_fee so the lot basis is not silently short.
3. Leave the fee's cash leg UNPOSTED. The money is not knowable as a posted sum yet, and §4.9 says an unknown is named, not guessed.
4. The blanket assertion suppression is a separate defect and is filed separately - option 2 looked worse than it is only because of it.
5. Deciding between per-row rounding and accumulated sub-kopek settlement needs one live sequence with balances immediately before and after a single fee, or the tariff's rounding clause. Blocked on the owner, like iaam-mnz.

Parts 1-3 are implementable now and are what the next worker gets.

title: C3: intraday order comes from the source
description: EffectiveOrder is (Date, u32) (dates.rs:122) and append_event_in_order overwrites sequence with MAX+1 (events.rs:46), so order within a day is insertion order. Facts that carry a source timestamp must keep the source's order, including when an earlier trade is discovered after later ones are already recorded. Nanoseconds do not fit u32, so the representation is part of the design, not of the plan. Acceptance: permuting the source response does not change projected FIFO order; a later-arriving earlier trade lands before events already recorded; equal timestamps have a deterministic, stated tie-break.
close_reason:
Implemented by an omp worker and accepted on the diff. EffectiveOrder gains source_time: Option<Time> with a hand-written Ord: within a day, timed events sort before untimed ones, and the doc comment states this is a chosen convention rather than a derived time, because §4.9 forbids inventing a time for an event that has none. EffectiveOrder::new(date, sequence) is unchanged, so all 44 existing call sites keep meaning 'the source gave no time'; with_source_time is the new constructor.

Equal source times are broken by raw_hash before sequence, so a re-import with a different response order produces the same order. The worker factored the two Rust sorting sites into one compare_for_replay in iaam-core/src/event/mod.rs rather than duplicating the rule, which is better than the brief asked for; the SQL in iaam-store/src/events.rs mirrors it exactly (source_time IS NULL first, so timed sorts first).

Three versions moved: event SCHEMA_VERSION 4 to 5, PROJECTION_VERSION 7 to 8, store SCHEMA_VERSION 12 to 13 with migration 0013 adding the nullable column.

Verified by the coordinator: architecture guard passes; 39 selected tests pass, including timed_events_sort_before_untimed_events (built as timed 23:59:59 with sequence 99 against untimed sequence 0, so a wrong direction or a sequence-driven order would fail it), equal_source_times_use_the_raw_hash_before_sequence, old_effective_order_payload_defaults_to_untimed, mixed_day_projection_is_reproducible, source_time_migration_preserves_preexisting_rows, and import_order_never_changes_the_projection.

Not run here by instruction: full suite, make check, mutants — the coordinator's end-of-epic gate.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Design note from the coordinator, to be verified when C3 is designed: a source-derived intraday sequence IS representable in the existing u32 without widening EffectiveOrder. Milliseconds since midnight are 0..86_399_999, and u32 holds up to 4_294_967_295, so ms*16 + collision_index (86_400_000*16 = 1_382_400_000) fits with four bits left for a deterministic tie-break of up to 16 events in the same millisecond. That is one candidate, not the decision — the alternatives (a separate time field, or a comparator that does not encode time into sequence) have to be weighed against the UNIQUE INDEX events_by_order (owner, effective_date, sequence) in 0001_initial.sql:31, which makes any collision an insertion failure rather than a reordering. The harder half of C3 is not the representation: append_event_in_order overwrites whatever sequence it is given (events.rs:46), and a trade discovered after later ones are already stored must still land before them.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Codex reviewed the proposal (add source_time to EffectiveOrder rather than encoding time into sequence). Verdict: safe with four named corrections. Do this one before C4.

1. Derived Option ordering is wrong. None sorts before Some, so an untimed coupon would be applied before every timed trade that day, which changes real accounting: with no lot yet it becomes unallocated_income (lots.rs:386,410), and in the cash perimeter an untimed inflow placed before a timed purchase hides a same-day negative-cash span that the reverse order records (perimeter.rs:227,248). Untimed events need an explicit ordering policy, not whatever derive(Ord) gives.
2. Equal source times are still nondeterministic: the store replaces sequence with insertion order (events.rs:53) and normalisation mints random event ids (operation.rs:173), so two equal-time fills swap when the response order swaps. The tie-break must come from the source - T-Invest supplies a stable trade number next to the timestamp (operations.proto:521).
3. Versions move: event SCHEMA_VERSION (event/mod.rs:142), store migration 12 with store SCHEMA_VERSION 12 (iaam-store/src/schema.rs:11), and PROJECTION_VERSION, because snapshot boundaries carry EffectiveOrder and incremental projection partitions on it (projection/mod.rs:136,317). Old CBOR reads the absent optional as None, and snapshots.rs:62 already treats an incompatible body as a cache miss. prefix_digest changes too, since it hashes the serialized event (projection/state.rs:241).
4. Existing comparison sites need no work: correction.rs:100 and perimeter.rs:227 compare EffectiveOrder as a value.

title: C2: PossibleDuplicate reaches the owner
description: sync_broker (sync.rs:98-105) branches only on Duplicate and drops the possible-duplicate verdict into an ordinary append. The decision must be threaded through: the event is still recorded (records_the_row() is true, dedup.rs:160-165) AND the pair reaches the caller. Touches SyncOutcome, the verdict type and the server DTO (dto.rs:3137). Acceptance: a row whose strong key does not match but whose fingerprint does is recorded and reported as a pair with the existing event id; the wire shape is specified and contract-tested.
close_reason:
Implemented by an omp worker and accepted on the diff, not on the report. Verdict::PossibleDuplicate { event, of, level } added (verdict.rs), threaded through sync_broker so the event is still appended and the pair is reported (sync.rs), counted as SyncOutcome.possible_duplicates, and exposed by the transport as of_event_id plus the numeric §10.6 level (dto.rs, contract.rs). Four exhaustive Verdict matches updated; checked by hand that no wildcard arm anywhere swallows the new variant, which the compiler would not have caught.

Verified by the coordinator, not taken on trust: cargo check -p iaam-ingest -p iaam-app -p iaam-server --all-targets finished clean in 15.36s, and the three new tests pass — a_fingerprint_match_is_recorded_as_a_possible_duplicate, a_renumbered_operation_is_recorded_as_a_possible_duplicate, mixed_sync_counts_possible_duplicates_separately_from_duplicates.

One rework was requested and delivered: the first fingerprint test set source_operation_id to None, which models 'no identifier' rather than the scenario this work exists for — a renumbered operation. The added test uses a different identifier and asserts its own premise with assert_ne! before asserting the outcome.

Not run here by instruction: the full suite, make check and mutants. Those are the coordinator's end-of-epic gate.

title: C1: fact identity is scoped by account
description: Dedup identity must include the account. Touches KnownRecord (dedup.rs:129-137), the source-id match (dedup.rs:246), find_duplicate (events.rs:162-175) and the UNIQUE INDEX events_source_operation (0001_initial.sql:40, owner-global today), which needs a migration. Care required: this is not a pure narrowing. A genuinely cross-account fact reported from both account views — EventKind::CashTransfer names both accounts by design (kind.rs:149) — must not be resurrected as two facts. Acceptance: two accounts of one source carrying the same source operation id both record; a transfer reported from both sides still records once; existing data migrates without loss.
close_reason:
Implemented by an omp worker and accepted on the diff. IdentityScope { Source, Account } lives in iaam-core (reconciliation/evidence.rs, next to SourceChannel); DocumentContext and KnownRecord carry the account; matches_key and the store's find_duplicate both honour the scope; migration 0012 recreates events_source_operation as (owner, source, account, source_operation_id). The BrokerChannel port declares the scope and the T-Invest channel returns Account; every other call site states Source explicitly, so no existing channel changed behaviour.

One rework, and the cause was my brief: I told the worker to put IdentityScope in iaam-ingest, which forced iaam-store to depend on it. scripts/check-architecture.sh catches exactly that ('iaam-store depends on higher-level layers: iaam-ingest, §3.2') while cargo check and clippy both pass clean — the brief had not required the guard. Moving the type to iaam-core fixed it; the guard now passes. Lesson recorded as lesson-a-worker-brief-that-names-only-cargo.

Verified by the coordinator: architecture guard passes, cargo check over four packages clean in 18.44s, 27 selected tests pass including account_scope_sync_records_same_source_identifier_for_two_accounts and account_scope_migration_preserves_preexisting_rows. The worker reported recovering two test files from edit-tool corruption; checked independently that no function was lost — dedup.rs went 47 to 55 declarations and sync.rs 19 to 28, with no name missing against HEAD.

Not run here by instruction: full suite, make check, mutants. Coordinator's end-of-epic gate.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Design note from the coordinator. Codex's round-two objection to C1 was that scoping identity by account is not a pure narrowing, because a genuinely cross-account fact reported from both account views could be resurrected as two facts — it named EventKind::CashTransfer, which is one fact naming both accounts (kind.rs:149-160).

Checked: CashTransfer carries its own transfer_id (kind.rs:156), so a transfer already has an identity independent of source_operation_id. That is the answer, and it avoids designing around a hypothesis nobody has observed.

Proposed shape, to be settled when C1 is designed: the uniqueness scope is a property the SOURCE declares, not a universal rule baked into the store. A channel states whether its operation identifier is unique per source or only per account; T-Invest is per account (operations.proto:485 also calls the id mutable), while a report channel keyed by document row is a different case entirely. The store then matches within the declared scope. This keeps the change from being a blanket rewrite of dedup semantics for every channel at once, which is what makes the migration risky.

title: [epic] Core prerequisites for per-trade facts
description:
Two rounds of adversarial review of the T-Invest per-trade design (iaam-d8b.23, spec .internal/specs/2026-08-31-tinkoff-execution-facts-design.md) established that the blocking problems are not in the channel. Expanding one broker row into N journal facts is unsafe until four core properties change. Each is independently verifiable and each is needed by every channel, not only T-Invest.

1. Fact identity does not know the account. dedup.rs:129-137 (KnownRecord has no account), sync.rs:84 (dedup runs before the store), 0001_initial.sql:40 (UNIQUE INDEX events_source_operation is owner-global). An operation identifier reused across two accounts of one source suppresses a legitimate fact, and the fix needs a migration, not just a narrower SELECT.

2. PossibleDuplicate never reaches the owner. sync.rs:98-105 branches only on Duplicate; the possible-duplicate verdict falls through to an ordinary append with no relation recorded and no pair returned. The second tier of §10.6 (dedup.rs:217-225) is inert at this call site, so every identity argument that leans on it is currently false.

3. Intraday order comes from insertion, not from the source. dates.rs:122 (EffectiveOrder is (Date, u32)), events.rs:46 (append overwrites sequence with MAX+1). N same-day facts therefore inherit the order the channel happened to return them in, which makes FIFO lot selection and realised result depend on response ordering.

4. Money is representable only in minor units, while a fee must be both exact and exactly equal to the cash leg. money.rs:60 (Money is minor-unit i64), event/mod.rs:352 (require_equal(cash_money, trade_settlement(gross, fee, accrued))), parse.rs:350 (NonRepresentableFraction). T-Invest withholds commissions at nano precision, so today a purchase with such a commission is refused in full (verified: tinkoff_mapping.rs:45-52, adapters/tinkoff.rs:526-546).

Blocks iaam-d8b.23.
close_reason:
All four children closed. The core can now carry per-trade facts: identity is scoped the way each source guarantees it (C1, with migration 0012), a possible duplicate reaches the owner instead of being silently appended (C2), intraday order comes from the source's timestamp rather than from insertion order (C3, migration 0013), and a commission reaches the lot basis without inventing a cash movement (C4).

Versions moved: event SCHEMA_VERSION 4 to 6, PROJECTION_VERSION 7 to 8, store SCHEMA_VERSION 11 to 13, TINKOFF_PARSER_VERSION /1 to /2.

End-of-epic gate, run by the coordinator: make check EXIT=0, 1557 tests, 0 failed. Two gate failures were found and fixed rather than worked around - the pinned version assertion in the health contract test (deliberately hardcoded so a bump cannot pass silently) and three migration tests that fabricated their starting database with PRAGMA user_version instead of applying the real migrations, which broke as soon as a migration touched events. The migration list now lives in one shared test helper.

Effect worth naming: the SBER purchase in the recorded fixture now reaches the journal. Before this epic the T-Invest channel accepted only cash deposits.

Deliberately left undone and filed: the fee's own cash movement is unposted because the broker's settlement rule is unknown (recorded on iaam-7xe8, needs a live sequence); iaam-dbvu covers quarantined rows suppressing every portfolio assertion. iaam-d8b.23 remains blocked pending a revision 3 of its spec, which can now be written against the changed core.

title: S9: stress-test gate
close_reason: Superseded by two full adversarial codex rounds against the written spec, which is a stronger gate than the stress-test offer at this point: round one killed five sections of revision 1, round two killed seven of revision 2 and returned 'not safe to write a plan from'.

title: S7: spec self-review
close_reason: Self-review done: no placeholders; §7 (fee_minor None), §9 option 2 (refuse only fields that become journal figures) and §4 (gross refused when not representable) are consistent; §8 accrued-interest branches match §13 test 9; §12 wording fixed to name one new glossary section instead of two. Scope is one epic in two files plus a fixture, which fits a single plan.

title: S10: transition to writing-plans
close_reason: Not reached, and deliberately so: the spec is blocked by iaam-jdmc (core prerequisites). Writing an implementation plan from a spec whose identity, commission, money and ordering sections rest on core behaviour that is about to change would produce a plan that has to be thrown away.

title: S6: write the spec to .internal/specs
close_reason: Spec written to .internal/specs/2026-08-31-tinkoff-execution-facts-design.md (515 lines). Covers seven findings: state never checked, order date passed off as trade date, commission counted twice, row identity on a mutable id, non-trading operations dated as trades, accrued interest dropped, and the open §3.4 conflict with nano-precision commissions.

title: S8: owner reviews the spec
close_reason: The owner did not read the spec file itself; the review that mattered came from two adversarial codex rounds, and the owner acted on their results — choosing one spec over splitting, then choosing core-first once round two showed the blockers were in the core rather than in the channel.

title: S5: present design by sections
close_reason: Sections 1 and 2 were presented and approved by the owner; the remaining sections were superseded when the owner asked for the whole spec at once and for codex review instead of section-by-section approval.

title: S1: explore project context and KB
close_reason: Context and KB gathered. KB check: 9 hits, 9 read. Folded in: iaam-d8b.22 (the Finam twin - settlement date must not be substituted by the trade date, absence yields None per §4.9, and a parsing-semantics change bumps the parser version) and iaam-d8b.14 (Tinkoff currently gives an honest 'unprovable' for settlement dates; SettlementLagPolicy is deliberately empty because 'usually T+1' is not evidence). Ruled out: tinkoff-sandbox-token, lesson-iaam-sourcechannel-sourceid, iaam-7b6/ADR-0002, iaam-46a, iaam-go9r, iaam-8dh, lesson-eventkind - none touch operation state or execution dates. Code facts: iaam-ingest/src/operation.rs:161 already rejects an event with no date at all, so refusing to substitute the order date degrades to a named verdict rather than silent loss; effective_date() priority is settled -> cash_posted -> paid -> trade (crates/iaam-core/src/dates.rs:103).

title: S4: 2-3 approaches with trade-offs
close_reason: Approaches were settled by the owner's answer plus the source contract rather than by a menu: per-trade facts (chosen), aggregate-per-order and last-trade-date (both rejected because they lose the per-lot detail that return calculation needs). The remaining design choice - how row identity survives an operation id that the contract itself calls mutable - is presented in the design sections.

title: S2: visual companion offer (just-in-time)
close_reason: Not applicable: the design questions here are about fact semantics in an append-only journal, none of which is clearer shown than described. Per the skill, the visual companion is never offered when no visual question arises.

title: S3: clarifying questions to the owner
close_reason: Owner answered two decisive questions. (1) Every trade must reach the journal individually - 'нам нужны все сделки с каждым лотом, иначе мы не посчитаем доходность' - so one order becomes N facts, not one aggregate. (2) The double-counted commission is fixed inside this epic rather than deferred. The owner also redirected the third question to the source contract: orders are irrelevant, we read operations, and an operation carries its executed trades. docs/api/tinkoff-invest/operations.proto settles it - OPERATION_STATE_EXECUTED means 'исполнена частично или полностью', so state alone never proves completeness and trades_info is the evidence.

title: Brainstorming: T-Invest operation state and execution date (iaam-d8b.23)
close_reason: Brainstorming complete, with a negative-but-decisive result. The spec .internal/specs/2026-08-31-tinkoff-execution-facts-design.md reached revision 2 and failed two adversarial codex rounds; both rounds' findings were verified against the code before being accepted. The outcome is that the T-Invest design is blocked on four core properties, now tracked as epic iaam-jdmc (C1 account-scoped identity, C2 PossibleDuplicate reaching the owner, C3 source-defined intraday order, C4 an exact fee that still equals its cash leg). Seven channel defects and five core defects are documented in the spec and on iaam-d8b.23. The owner chose core-first; implementation started with C2.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Self-check during codex review found a defect in §7 of the spec BEFORE the review returned. Dropping fee_minor and letting the commission arrive only as a separate Fee fact silently lowers the lot basis: crates/iaam-core/src/projection/lots.rs:774-777 adds the trade fee into acquired_basis and cost_basis, and the test a_purchase_creates_a_lot_including_the_fee (lots.rs:1833) states the rule as §7.2 - commission is included in acquisition cost, accrued interest is not. EventKind::Fee is documented as 'Fee not tied to a trade' (event/kind.rs:174), so a standalone fee never reaches the lot. §7 must be rewritten: the commission has to reach the trade, and the double count is resolved by allocating the order-level commission across its trades pro rata by quantity, with §3.4 applied to the result and an explicit remainder rule.

title: Вычисление доли разнесения нарушает заслон архитектуры: денежная арифметика в iaam-app
description:
make check падает на scripts/check-architecture.sh:

  АРХИТЕКТУРА: денежная арифметика в оболочке (crates/iaam-app/src):
  число в ответе обязано приходить из ядра (§3.1, §13)
  crates/iaam-app/src/allocation.rs:62  checked_add
  crates/iaam-app/src/allocation.rs:71  checked_sub
  crates/iaam-app/src/allocation.rs:91  checked_mul

Внесено T11 (2420fae). Заслон ищет try_add/try_sub/checked_add/checked_sub/checked_mul/checked_negate в crates/iaam-app/src и crates/iaam-server/src. Приёмка iaam-ingest исключена намеренно — она собирает факт из полей источника, а не вычисляет.

Причина: план эпика и задание воркеру говорили только «вычисление живёт в приложении, а не в приёмке» — верно про iaam-ingest и неверно про iaam-app. Заслон не гонялся ни разу до T13, потому что ворота задач были точечными.

## Что делать

resolve_basis_allocation целиком работает на типах ядра (PerUnitAmount, Date, BondSchedule, BasisAllocation, ReturnedShare, AllocationEvidence) — в iaam-app её ничто не держит. Перенести вычисление в crates/iaam-core/src/rules/ рядом с amortisation.rs: это версионированное правило (ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM_V1), там его место по смыслу, а не только по заслону.

В iaam-app остаётся то, ради чего оно там и оказалось: чтение снимка графика из MarketStore, сборка BondSchedule и вызов правила. Арифметики в нём не остаётся.

iaam-ingest по-прежнему получает готовое JournalEventEnrichment и хранилища не видит — это свойство T11 сохранить.

Тесты вычисления переезжают вместе с ним.

## Acceptance Criteria

- make check зелёный целиком (сейчас падает на шаге arch).
- В crates/iaam-app/src нет вызовов checked_*/try_* денежной арифметики.
- iaam-ingest не зависит от хранилища и справочника.
- Все тесты вычисления сохранены и зелёные; поведение не изменилось.
close_reason: resolve_basis_allocation переехала в crates/iaam-core/src/rules/allocation.rs, поведение не менялось; make check EXIT=0 (bb18b2b)

description:

notes:
НАЙДЕНО ПРИ ЗАКРЫТИИ T13/24.2 — заслон check-architecture.sh слеп к разыменованию.

strip_comments() (scripts/check-architecture.sh:25-31) отбрасывает строку, если после отступа стоит '*' — считает её продолжением блочного комментария. В Rust так выглядит присваивание через разыменование, и оно из проверки выпадает целиком.

Проверено: 'crates/iaam-app/src/jobs.rs:230: *current = current.checked_add(delta).unwrap_or(*current);' греп заслона находит, а strip_comments съедает, и заслон рапортует 'пройдены'. То есть '*total = total.checked_add(money)' в оболочке заслон не увидит никогда.

Сам jobs.rs:230 нарушением не является: там суммируются количества (Dec) ради выбора инструментов для синхронизации, а не деньги в ответе API. Чинить надо заслон, а не эту строку.

Как чинить: отличать комментарий от кода не по первому символу. Минимально — требовать, чтобы после '*' шёл пробел или конец строки ('* ' и '*/' — комментарий, '*current' — код). Заодно проверить остальные ветки strip_comments на тот же класс ложного срабатывания и завести тест на сам заслон: строка с '*x = y.checked_add(z)' обязана его ронять.
close_reason: Три модуля в мутационном заслоне (18 мутантов, 0 выживших); заслон архитектуры починен и проверяет себя; active_instruments переехала в ядро; make check EXIT=0 (bed9434)
