Обнаружено при исполнении задачи 20, когда писался приёмочный тест эпика lots_disagreeing_with_positions_abort_the_projection: первая редакция теста строила именно такую фантомную позицию, и инвариант её пропустил.

На сегодня дыра недостижима через журнал: и покупка, и восстановленная позиция создают запись в книге, а структурная проверка не пропускает событие, чья нога противоречит типу. Но инвариант — второй рубеж, и он обязан ловить состояние, а не полагаться на первый рубеж.
acceptance_criteria:
- Обход идёт по объединению ключей книги лотов и позиций, а не только по книге
- Позиция без записи в книге даёт LotsDoNotMatchPosition
- Тест строит именно такое состояние и проверяет отказ
close_reason: Обход в invariants::check идёт по объединению ключей книги лотов и позиций (f02934d, влито). Позиция без записи в книге даёт LotsDoNotMatchPosition. Добавлен отдельный тест a_position_without_a_single_lot_is_caught; исходный lots_disagreeing_with_positions_abort_the_projection сохранён без изменений — первая редакция воркера переписывала его вместо добавления, случай расхождения по одной бумаге при этом терялся, работа возвращена на доработку и исправлена. 6 тестов модуля зелёные на объединённом дереве.

title: Тест на конкурентную запись: два одновременных запроса за одним порядковым номером
description: Гонка выдачи порядкового номера закрыта транзакцией с немедленным захватом и уникальным индексом (owner, effective_date, sequence). Проверено рассуждением и схемой, но не нагрузочным тестом. Стоит написать при появлении второго писателя.
acceptance_criteria:
- Тест поднимает два параллельных писателя на одну базу
- Ни один порядковый номер не выдан дважды; при коллизии видна ошибка, а не тихая перестановка
close_reason:
Тест конкурентной выдачи порядкового номера принят (ce3b0c8, влито). Два писателя, два отдельных SqliteStore на один файл (база в памяти между соединениями не разделяется), старт по барьеру, временный файл удаляется. Проверяются три вещи: ни один sequence не выдан дважды, число строк равно числу успешных ответов, успешные номера образуют 1..=N без пропусков. Принимаются оба законных исхода — оба успели, либо один получил ошибку занятости.

Тест проверен фальсификацией координатором: чтение MAX(sequence) вынесено ИЗ транзакции (та самая гонка из doc-комментария метода) плюс снята уникальность индекса events_by_order — тест краснеет 10 раз из 10. На верном коде 10 зелёных из 10.

Первая фальсификация координатора была неверной: замена Immediate на Deferred даёт SQLITE_BUSY, а не задвоенный номер, поэтому тест не мог покраснеть в принципе. Из-за этой ошибки работа была ошибочно отправлена на переделку и слияние откачено; обе оценки отменены, тест принят в исходном виде.

title: Интервальный XIRR: требует ряда NAV на начало интервала
description:
XIRR is reported over an account's whole history, never over a requested
interval. The reason is stated in `crates/iaam-core/src/returns/mod.rs`: an
interval return needs an opening NAV valuation as its first cash flow, and
stage 1 values a portfolio only as of the report date. Substituting cost basis
for the opening value would present as a return a figure that corresponds to no
transaction.

So this is blocked on valuation, not on the solver: it needs a NAV series — a
valuation as of an arbitrary past date — which in turn needs stored price
history at that date (E3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A return report can be requested for an interval, and its first flow is a
  real opening valuation, not cost basis.
- Where no valuation can be produced for the interval's opening date, the
  report refuses with a named reason rather than substituting anything.
- The whole-history report keeps its current meaning and is not redefined as an
  interval starting at the first movement.

title: An account has two views on purpose, and it will read as an oversight
description:
`AccountView` (crates/iaam-app/src/ports.rs) is unchanged by iaam-34f3; the new fields live on a sibling `AccountDetailView` with its own port methods. The immediate cause was mechanical — `AccountView` is built at thirteen sites, six of them inside files another agent held — but the result is better than the unified alternative and should not be quietly undone.

The action policy and the reports read `AccountView`. The cash class is a label decision 0004 §3 forbids any rule from branching on. Keeping it off the view those two read makes the prohibition structural rather than a comment somebody has to obey.

Filed so that a later reader who finds two account views does not merge them as duplication.
design:
Either keep the split and say so where it will be read — a doc comment on both types naming the other and the reason — or unify and accept that the prohibition returns to being prose. Prefer the first.

If unified anyway, the thirteen construction sites in actions.rs and reports.rs must be updated, which is the work this deferred.

title: An account's identity, aliases and class can only be set when it is created
description:
Migration 0020 added `provider`, `provider_account_id` and `cash_class` to accounts, and `PUT /v1/accounts/{id}/aliases` maintains the alias set. Nothing maintains the other three: they are write-once at `POST /v1/accounts`, and the upsert path deliberately ignores them on a repeat create because that call is idempotent rather than an update.

So an account that already exists — every account the owner has today — can never acquire an external identity or a class. Found while implementing iaam-34f3.
design:
One route in the shape of the alias one, replacing the declared fields rather than patching them. Two questions it must answer:

- **Changing an identity is not the same as setting one.** Setting an identity on an account that had none is ordinary. Changing one that facts were already imported under points the account at a different source, and the rows recorded under the old identity do not move. Refuse the change, or accept it and say in the response what it did not do.
- `cash_class` is a label nothing branches on (decision 0004 §3), so changing it is safe and needs no ceremony beyond the owner's word.

title: Twelve accounts is twelve calls to state transfer partners, and symmetry cannot fix it
description:
There is no batch form of `PUT /v1/accounts/{id}/transfer-partners`; the queue emits one item per account and each is its own call.

The obvious shortcut does not work, and the reason is worth recording because it will be proposed again. **Making the relation symmetric cannot halve the calls.** The store writes directed rows and no reciprocal (`crates/iaam-store/src/reference.rs:672`), and `transfer_relationships_completion` (crates/iaam-app/src/actions.rs:1311) matches on `statement.account == account` alone, its doc saying so outright: being named as somebody else's partner does not satisfy an account's own statement.

That is correct, because the question is not the pairwise assertion «is A related to B». It is an **enumeration with closure** — «these, and no others». Naming B inside A's enumeration establishes A↔B and says nothing about whether B also moves money with C. Auto-closing B's question from A's answer would assert that B has no partners beyond those already named, which is a fabricated fact about the owner's money of exactly the kind this system refuses everywhere else. A completeness statement per account is irreducible.

What is reducible is the transport. Found while fixing iaam-9hkc.
design:
A thin batch: one route carrying `{account, partners}[]`, validated exactly as the single form validates (self-reference, existence, dedup — crates/iaam-server/src/routes.rs:1663) and applied atomically. `record_account_transfer_statement` already replaces per account inside one immediate transaction, so the store needs nothing new.

Two questions to settle first:

- **Does the queue name the batch?** The frontier emits one item per account, each with its own preset `/account` and its own `/partners`. A single item covering many accounts needs a `RequestPlan` whose `missing` pointers address array elements — a shape nothing else uses. The cheap alternative is that the per-account items stay and the batch is a client convenience the queue never names, losing only the agent's ability to discover it. Prefer the cheap one unless the array-pointer shape is wanted for other reasons.
- **Partial failure.** One named account the owner does not hold must reject the whole batch, matching the existing «refused rather than ignored» rule at routes.rs:1674.

Sequence this after iaam-f8d3. Today nothing outside the frontier and the read-back DTO consumes these rows at all, so the ergonomics of stating them is not yet the binding cost.
close_reason:
PUT /v1/accounts/transfer-partners, a static sibling of the per-account route, following the /v1/instruments/resolve precedent. The response element is the existing AccountTransferPartnersDto, so a batch entry reads exactly as a single call's body, including the 'stated' field that separates 'none of my others' from 'he has not said'.

Validation was extracted into one function both routes call, rather than a second set that can drift. The store needed a batch method: record_account_transfer_statement opens its own transaction and commits, so twelve calls are twelve transactions and a failure on the fifth leaves four replaced and eight standing. Both forms now share one private write.

404 for an unknown account, not 400: the batch is a cheaper way to make the same twelve calls, and if twelve single calls would each have produced 404, one batch collapsing them must not turn 'no such account' into 'your document is malformed' — a caller must read the answer the same way whichever way it asked. 422 for an account named twice, since two enumerations for one account cannot both be the complete one.

The queue deliberately does not name the batch, and the decision is asserted so reversing it is deliberate. One item covering twelve accounts carries one ActionState for twelve independent questions, so answering eight of twelve would be inexpressible — collapsing the items re-introduces one layer up the very fabrication the directed relation refuses. Follow-up named for whoever owns actions.rs: a hint on the existing per-account item, leaving twelve items with twelve states.

title: Four action reasons assert that no operation exists without anyone having checked
description:
An audit of all fourteen `ActionKind`s (for iaam-ht3l) found four reasons that assert the API offers no remedy, each sitting beside a plausible route:

- `CoverageGapUnrepaired` — «no repair operation exists in this API», beside `POST /v1/accounts/{account}/repairs/custody` and `POST /v1/corrections/imports`.
- `IndependentConfirmationMissing` — «no acquisition operation exists in this API», beside `POST /v1/documents` and the import-session routes, which is how a second document from a different parser gets in.
- `DiscrepancyUnresolved` — «no resolution operation exists in this API», beside `POST /v1/corrections` and `POST /v1/reconciliation/balance`.
- `UnexplainedResidual` — says «no **report** operation can resolve it», which is verbatim the phrasing `undecomposed_outflows_action`'s own doc comment records as having been wrong there: «true and irrelevant — the action catalogue resolves a target against the whole completed contract, not a report-local namespace».

Each is internally consistent as prose: the reason names no remedy and the target publishes none. The question is whether the claim is true. A false «nothing here can help you» is the defect iaam-1lqx documents for `StartAccountImport`, and these are the four candidates for the same thing.

Separately, `ResolveTransferRelationships` names two ways out — «name the accounts, or record that none of your others is on the other side» — and publishes one operation, which is correct: `record_account_transfer_partners` serves both, the second being `partners: []`. But nothing in the published plan says an empty array is admissible, while `RecordAccountTransferPartnersRequest`'s own doc says the empty list and not calling the route mean different things. That one is fixed with an `InputAlternative` on `/partners`, not a second operation.
design:
Four verifications, then at most four small changes. For each: does the named route actually close this item? If yes, the item is promoted the way iaam-1lqx promotes StartAccountImport. If no, the reason keeps its claim and gains the half-sentence saying why the obvious route is not it — which is the part a reader currently has to supply from nothing.

Do this after iaam-1lqx, which establishes the pattern on the clearest case.
notes: Correction: the StartAccountImport bead this references is iaam-eu73, not iaam-1lqx (an id that does not exist).
close_reason:
Four verdicts, each traced to what actually removes the item from the ledger rather than to what the route is named.

CoverageGapUnrepaired — claim kept. repair_custody's entire predicate is is_affected_trade (a Trade with a quantity leg whose custody equals the account), and retracting a trade cannot record a row that was never parsed. correct_import would reverse the coverage-gap event itself along with every row of that import that did arrive, so the item would stop being published because the record of the refusal was withdrawn. Half-sentence added.

IndependentConfirmationMissing — promoted for cash and positions, kept blocked for tax basis and income. Ground::BrokerApiAgreesWithStatement promotes only those two dimensions, and sync writes a ControlAssertion under its own parser version and document hash, so is_independent_of holds against any statement channel. POST /v1/documents also closes it but cannot be published: the OpenAPI dump shows upload_document with content=[text/plain] and no JSON schema, so registering it would fail the catalog build. It stays in the reason. The import-session routes are not a remedy at all — a commit adds no assertion group.

DiscrepancyUnresolved — promoted. POST /v1/corrections closes it from either side. POST /v1/reconciliation/balance does not: merge_status keeps Discrepant from either side on purpose.

UnexplainedResidual — claim kept, 'no report operation' dropped. A residual names no event, and every operation that could move it is addressed to an event the caller names.

title: policy_version is a literal 1 in one route, and absent from the four others that publish actions
description:
`ActionsResponseDto` publishes `policy_version` so a client knows which policy computed the items (crates/iaam-server/src/dto.rs:2908). Two things are wrong with it.

**It is never set.** `policy_version` occurs exactly once outside the type: `policy_version: 1` hardcoded at crates/iaam-server/src/routes.rs:126. Nothing derives it, nothing bumps it. A version that cannot change tells a client nothing, and when the policy does change — new ActionKind, changed category, changed reason — the field will still read 1.

**Four of the five places that publish actions omit it.** `actions: Vec<ActionDto>` is embedded in three further DTOs (dto.rs:2314, :4751, :5180) — the reconciliation response, the broker sync outcome and the money-flow report — none carrying a version. So the same computed list arrives versioned down one route and unversioned down three.

Found while documenting the list-response convention (iaam-1y2j). The audit that produced it found no violation of that rule anywhere else: every list route already conforms.
design:
Decide whether the version is worth keeping before wiring it anywhere.

If it is: derive it from something that actually moves — the `ActionKind` set, the policy module's own constant bumped by whoever changes a category — and publish it wherever `ActionDto` is published, which means it belongs on a wrapper around the embedded lists too, not only on the top-level route.

If it is not: remove it. A field a client is invited to branch on, which is a literal that never changes, is worse than no field. Note that removing it changes `ActionsResponseDto` from a wrapper to a bare array under the rule now documented in docs/api/conventions.md — which would be the rule working, not an exception to it.

title: List endpoints disagree about whether a list is an array or an object
description:
`GET /v1/accounts` returns a bare `[AccountDto]`, as do instruments, categories, category groups, classification rules and the rest. `GET /v1/actions` returns `{policy_version, items}` and `GET /v1/journal/events` returns a `JournalPageDto`. Both wrappers have a reason — a policy version, a page cursor — and neither reason is visible from the outside, so a client guesses per endpoint.

Reported by an external reviewer as friction rather than a bug, which is what it is.
design:
Pick the rule and write it down in the API document rather than retrofitting a wrapper everywhere:

> A list is a bare array unless the response carries something about the list itself — a page cursor, a version the items were computed under — in which case it is an object with `items` and that something.

Then check every list route against it. The bare-array ones are almost certainly all correct under that rule; the value is that a client can predict the shape without opening the specification. Adding a wrapper to `GET /v1/accounts` is a breaking change for no gain.
close_reason: The rule is documented in docs/api/conventions.md and every list route was audited against it: 33 routes, zero violations. The shapes were already deliberate — BalancesReportDto's own doc comment states the rule in miniature — they simply had no public statement. The reviewer's item was friction, not a defect, and it is answered. Two follow-ups filed separately; a third duplicated iaam-ewcl.

title: An action needing the owner but offering no operation is indistinguishable from one the agent can run
description:
Found by codex while reviewing the multi-bank feedback; verified in the tree.

`start_account_import_action` (crates/iaam-app/src/actions.rs) is
`state: ActionState::NeedsOwnerInput` with `ActionTarget::None`. Both readings
are true of it — the owner must fetch a statement, and no operation exists — but
`Blocked` is documented as exactly the second, and `NeedsOwnerInput` elsewhere
in the queue accompanies a real operation with a `missing` list.

For an agent that is the difference between "collect these fields and call this"
and "there is nothing here for you to call".

Minor, and named because the queue's states are the agent's only map of what it
may do.
acceptance_criteria:
- An item with no operation target is either given one or reported as `blocked`, whose own doc comment says 'No operation in this API is available for this item'.
- An agent reading the queue can tell what it may call from what it must wait on, without inspecting the target.
close_reason: start_account_import is blocked with no target and no scope; typed subject added to the action envelope. 805f957

title: Whether §11 reaches the money-flow report and the action queue is unexamined
description:
iaam-sbht wired perimeter::assess into the balances answer and the reconciliation ledger. Two period-shaped surfaces were left untouched and deliberately unexamined, both because they were another worker's files at the time:

- crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/reports.rs, money_flow. It is a period report and §11 arguably reaches it, but nothing decides whether a §11-blocking account should be marked there too.
- The action queue. A blocking classification is exactly the kind of state that ought to reach the owner as something to act on, and no action is emitted for it today.

This is a question before it is a task: neither surface should gain a marker until it is settled that §11 means the same thing there as it does on the balances answer.
acceptance_criteria: It is decided and recorded whether §11 marks the money-flow report and whether it produces an action; whichever way, the reason is written down.

title: The claim answer still publishes the balance point as a bare string
description: iaam-dfoh typed the request side: OwnerBalanceRequest.at is now BalancePointDto, published with a sentence per code. ClaimDto::CashBalance and ClaimDto::PositionQuantity (crates/iaam-server/src/dto.rs) still declare it as a String, filled from at.code().to_owned() in claim_dto — the same value and the same two codes, one direction later, on the answer side. BalancePointDto::from_domain already exists and drops straight in. Surfaced by the worker on iaam-dfoh, whose brief did not assign that type either way.
acceptance_criteria: A claim in a reconciliation answer publishes the balance point as the enumeration, with the same two codes and the same wire form; a schema assertion covers it.

title: The balance point travels as a bare string although it has exactly two values
description:
`OwnerBalanceRequest.at` is `pub at: String` (crates/iaam-server/src/dto.rs:4165). The domain type is `BalancePoint` with exactly two variants and a `code()` — `opening` and `closing` (crates/iaam-core/src/reconciliation/claim.rs:60). So the contract publishes a free string where it could publish the enumeration, and a caller that guesses `open` or `start` learns the permitted values only by being refused.

This is the same defect as iaam-oqhv one route over, and the fix is the same shape: a transport enum in `dto.rs` built like `CurrencyDto` and `AliasNamespaceDto`, with `to_domain()`/`from_domain()`. It matters a little more now than it did: the action queue is being changed to preset `at` at both points, so the value becomes something a caller reads out of an action and sends back.

Found while checking a live instance's action queue against the code.
acceptance_criteria: The generated OpenAPI enumerates opening and closing for this field; the serialised values are unchanged; a wrong value is refused as ApiError naming the field and the two valid codes.
close_reason: OwnerBalanceRequest.at is BalancePointDto, published through described_vocabulary with a sentence per code. Wire form unchanged; a preset read out of /v1/actions posts back verbatim, asserted by a test that sends no literal of its own.

title: The five namespace codes reach the contract without their meanings
description: utoipa 5.5 renders a plain unit-variant enum as {"type":"string","enum":[...]} and discards the per-variant doc comments, so `AliasNamespaceDto` publishes five codes and one enum-wide sentence. `crates/iaam-server/src/vocabulary.rs` already has `described_vocabulary` machinery — used by `VerdictCodeDto` and its neighbours — that publishes a oneOf with a meaning per code. The wire form would not change. Found by the worker on iaam-oqhv, who followed the CurrencyDto pattern the brief named and surfaced this rather than widening scope.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five namespace codes carries its own sentence in the generated document, by the same mechanism the verdict codes use.
close_reason: AliasNamespaceDto publishes through vocabulary::described_vocabulary, the mechanism the verdict codes use: a oneOf with a sentence per code, codes taken from the domain's own code() so the contract cannot drift. Wire form unchanged.

title: The fx response and the owner-supplied rate body still spell the currency pair from/to
description: iaam-nyp7 renamed the market/fx **query** to base/quote/from/to. Two bodies keep the old spelling: `FxRateDto` (crates/iaam-server/src/dto.rs:2588), a request body, and `MarketFxDto` (:2626), a response body. Neither carries an interval beside the pair, so neither has the collision that bead fixed — but an agent that asks for `base`/`quote` and reads `from`/`to` back is being taught two names for one thing. Found and deliberately left by the worker on iaam-nyp7, whose brief assigned dto.rs elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: One vocabulary for a currency pair across query, request body and response body, or a stated reason in the contract why the response differs.
close_reason: base/quote runs from the query through the request and response bodies to the scenario view. The store columns keep from_code/to_code: renaming them is a migration for a name the contract never published.

title: The reconciliation response does not name the account or range it answered
description:
ReconciliationResponseDto is { statuses, gaps } (crates/iaam-server/src/dto.rs:3921). The account and the range live on each status and each gap, so a response with no statuses and no gaps loses the question it answered entirely: an agent holding the body alone cannot say which account and which period came back empty.

The handler has both — they are query parameters (crates/iaam-server/src/routes.rs:413) — and does not copy them into the response.

Found while designing E9.T5 (iaam-7zbb), which needs the account filter applied where the items are built rather than checked against the envelope afterwards.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read reconciliation for an account and range with no statuses and no gaps.
2. The body is `{ statuses: [], gaps: [] }`: an agent holding it alone cannot say which account and which period came back empty, although the handler had both as query parameters.
acceptance_criteria:
- The reconciliation response names the account and the range it answered, so a body with no statuses and no gaps still says which question came back empty.
- The values come from the handler's own query parameters, which already hold them.
- The account filter is applied where the items are built, not checked against the envelope afterwards (E9.T5).

title: flow_diagnostics panics when a report aggregate overflows
description:
iaam-app::actions::flow_diagnostics expects() both not_decomposed_by_account and residuals_by_account. Its signature is -> Vec<Action> with no error channel, fixed by the E9.T4 design, so a report whose aggregates overflow takes down the request instead of returning an error.

Every other path through MoneyFlow returns Result<_, MoneyFlowError> and the transport turns it into a refusal. This one does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a money-flow report whose per-account aggregates overflow.
2. `flow_diagnostics` panics on its `expect()` instead of returning an error, and the request dies rather than refusing.
acceptance_criteria:
- `flow_diagnostics` returns a result rather than panicking: a report whose aggregates overflow produces a refusal, as every other path through `MoneyFlow` does.
- No `expect()` remains on that path.
- Covered by a test that overflows an aggregate and asserts a refusal, not a panic.

title: The owner can see the API and call it from a page
description:
The owner has no way to look at the API. The OpenAPI document is served at
`/v1/openapi.json` and is machine-readable; nothing renders it, and nothing lets
him send a request without a shell.

This is a VIEW of the generated document, not a second description, so it cannot
drift — which is why it is worth having at all.

## Which renderer, and why

`utoipa-swagger-ui` 9.0.2 (carries Swagger UI 5.17.14), with the `vendored`
feature. Its default build path shells out to system `curl` to download the
assets, which would make the build non-reproducible and network-dependent; the
`vendored` feature exists for exactly this and is documented as the answer for
networkless environments.

`utoipa-scalar` 0.3.0 was examined and rejected. Its `res/scalar.html` is 377
bytes and loads `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@scalar/api-reference` from a
third-party CDN with no version pin, at page load. That places unpinned foreign
JavaScript on the one page where the owner types an owner token, and it means
the page does not open at all without internet — for a tool that lives on the
loopback interface. Redoc renders but cannot send a request, which is the half
that was asked for.

Check at implementation time: the swagger-ui crate documents axum ">= 0.7" and
we are on 0.8.

## Two conditions

- **Off by default, enabled explicitly.** A subcommand flag or a variable, not
  always-on. The service is documented as not facing the internet directly, and
  a page with an execute button must not appear where nobody asked for it.
- **The Authorize dialog means an owner token in a browser.** ADR-0003 records
  that a credential in a browser is a different theft and XSS risk, and that a
  surface having its own credential buys attribution rather than containment. On
  loopback for a single owner this is acceptable, but as a decision rather than
  a side effect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The UI is served only when explicitly enabled, and the default is off.
- No network access during the build, and none when the page is opened: the
  assets ship in the binary.
- `make deps` stays green — the licence must pass `deny.toml`.
- The page renders the SAME document served at `/v1/openapi.json`; there is no
  second copy and no hand-written page.
- A request sent from the page reaches the API and is authorised like any other.
notes:
Checked upstream before deciding: juhaku/utoipa has no issue, open or closed, about the Scalar CDN dependency, offline use, version pinning or vendoring. So this is not a known problem awaiting a fix — it is the crate's design, and nothing suggests it will change.

Adjacent evidence found while looking: issue #1520 asks how to disable Scalar's 'Ask AI' button and AI agent. The CDN bundle therefore ships an AI feature of its own, loading on the page where the owner would type an owner token. The issue was closed with no comments, so whether it can be disabled is unknown.

Neither fact is a criticism of the crate for its intended use. Both matter here because our page is the one place a credential and third-party JavaScript would meet.
Decided 2026-09-02: utoipa-swagger-ui with the vendored feature. No upstream issue is being filed — the question was considered and dropped; the crate's behaviour is its design, and waiting on someone else's repository is not a plan.

title: The rate limit is announced, not discovered by hitting it
description:
A client learns the rate limit by hitting it. `IAAM_RATE_LIMIT` (120) and
`IAAM_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS` (60) are configured and enforced
(`crates/iaam-server/src/rate_limit.rs`), and nothing announces them, so an agent
pacing a batch import has to discover the wall by walking into it.

Noticed while reviewing draft-aiendpoint-ai-discovery, which carries a
`rate_limits` field. That draft is not adopted and is not being taken, but the
gap it names is real for us.

The IETF HTTPAPI working group has live work on RateLimit header fields, which
is the right shape: headers on the response that carry the limit, the remaining
quota and the reset. Check its current state before implementing — it was
in progress rather than ratified when this was filed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful response carries the current limit, what remains of it, and when
  the window resets, using the header names the RateLimit specification defines
  rather than invented ones.
- `429` carries the same, plus `Retry-After`.
- The values come from the running configuration, not from constants written
  twice.
- If the specification has still not settled, that is recorded here with the
  date checked, and the decision to wait or to adopt the draft names is explicit.

title: A classification question is a durable case, not a sentence
description:
`Verdict::NeedsClassification` carries a prose question and nothing else, and
production never constructs it. Before the API can ask the owner a typed
question, the answer needs somewhere to land: the question identifies no
durable case, names no rejected operation, and there is no path by which an
answer resubmits the work it blocked.

Held until that protocol exists. Attaching an address to this state earlier
would send an agent to a classification-rule endpoint with no way to connect the
rule it writes to the row that provoked the question.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A question is a durable case with an identity, naming the operation it blocks.
- The owner's answer, arriving through the agent, resolves that case and the
  blocked work is retried without the agent reconstructing it.
- Only then does the state carry an action.
notes:
Prior art, checked in source rather than docs: LangGraph's Interrupt carries exactly two fields — value (what the client is shown) and id, whose docstring says it 'can be used to resume the interrupt directly'. Resumption goes through Command(resume=...), which accepts a MAPPING of interrupt id to answer, not merely the next value in sequence (libs/langgraph/langgraph/types.py).

That is the minimum honest shape for our question: identity on the question, and the answer addressed to that identity. Positional correspondence breaks silently as soon as two questions are open at once, which is the normal case for a batch import. Not a dependency on LangChain — a precedent that the shape we need is the shape others converged on.

title: The daily close time is 19:00 with no timezone, so the market-closed threshold is wrong
description:
crates/iaam-app/src/jobs.rs:25 `default_close_time()` returns 19:00 and
jobs.rs:407 compares it against OffsetDateTime::now_utc(). 19:00 UTC is 22:00
MSK, so the threshold is already wrong for the market it was written for.
MarketSchedule::new accepts an override, but production only calls ::default()
(jobs.rs:183).

CORRECTION_WINDOW_DAYS = 21 and INITIAL_PADDING_DAYS = 7 (jobs.rs:20-22) are
reachable only the same way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The close time carries its timezone, or is compared in the market's own zone.
- The schedule is configurable by the deployer rather than only by a test.
- A test pins the boundary in a named timezone rather than in UTC by accident.

title: No GET /v1/contours: the contour composition is write-only over HTTP
description: crates/iaam-server/src/lib.rs:125 registers create_contour_version only. An import skill cannot ask which accounts are inside the contour, so the perimeter has to be handed to it as run-time input and cannot be checked against what the system believes. A read route would let a caller verify what it was told. See §2.1 of .internal/specs/2026-09-01-bank-import-skill-design.md (iaam-mksb).
acceptance_criteria:
- A read route answers which accounts are inside the contour, so an import skill can check the perimeter it was handed against what the system believes.
- It is a view of the same composition the write route builds, so the two cannot drift.
close_reason: GET /v1/contours and GET /v1/contours/{contour}, derived from the same composition the write routes build. 28842eb

title: Step 9: stress-test gate
close_reason: stress-test declined at the gate

title: Step 2: offer the visual companion just-in-time
close_reason: done: KB checked, input channels and integrity level settled with the owner

title: Cross-source equivalence: a fact recorded under another source row does not resolve an outstanding one
description:
From the E4 design (spec 2026-09-01). An outstanding source row is resolved only by a fact
carrying its own row key. If the same economic occurrence is recorded under a different
source row - a second broker report, a manual entry not targeting the row - the row stays
outstanding.

This is a conservative false taint and is preferred to the alternative: the journal cannot
prove two source rows describe the same occurrence from their legs alone, and matching on
'account + date + amount' is a natural key this code refuses by design (two identical
purchases in one day are legitimate, crates/iaam-store/src/events.rs find_duplicate).

Closing it needs explicit owner or importer equivalence, not inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Resolution by explicit equivalence — stated by the owner or by the importer — not by inference from legs.
- Matching on account, date and amount stays refused: two identical purchases in one day are legitimate.
- Until then the false taint is conservative and accepted; this bead records that it is deliberate.

title: A durable source-row namespace: SourceId is the broker access record, so reprovisioning orphans outstanding rows
description:
Evidence: crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/sqlite.rs:728 constructs the Tinkoff channel with
SourceId(access.id) - source identity IS the broker access record. Revoking and recreating
access changes the UUID while the broker account and its operation identifiers are unchanged.

Under the E4 model (spec 2026-09-01), an outstanding row is keyed by (SourceId, row name).
Rows recorded under the old access are therefore never matched by imports under the new one:
a false taint the owner must clear by hand.

A durable namespace would key on broker + environment + remote account rather than the
credential record. Deferred from E4 deliberately: it is its own change with its own
migration, and the failure mode is conservative.
acceptance_criteria:
- A source row's namespace keys on broker, environment and remote account rather than on the credential record.
- Revoking and recreating broker access no longer orphans outstanding rows recorded under the old access.
- Ships with its own migration: existing rows are carried into the durable namespace rather than abandoned.

title: Step 9: stress-test gate
close_reason: skipped: two adversarial codex rounds already killed two designs and reshaped the third — a stress-test pass would be weaker than what was run

title: Step 2: offer the visual companion just-in-time
close_reason: no visual question arose

title: A synchronisation that recorded only a coverage gap still moves the account's data-coverage dates
description:
Severity: Minor
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-core/src/projection/state.rs observe() counts every event and moves first_event, last_event and their per-account maps for any event carrying an effective date, without regard to kind. EventKind::ImportCoverageGap is dated CashPostedDate(to) like a control assertion, so it qualifies.

Consequence: a sync in which every row was refused and the portfolio was withheld records exactly one event - the gap - and the account then reports dated data coverage over an interval for which nothing at all was recorded. The fields are described as the boundaries of available data, and the gap is the assertion that data is missing.

Financially the event is inert: it has no legs, balances consume only legs, and lots, income and active instruments ignore it explicitly. It is projection-inert everywhere except the coverage counters. Found by an adversarial codex review of epic iaam-40vm.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Synchronise an interval in which every row is refused and the portfolio is withheld: exactly one event is recorded, the coverage gap.
2. Read the account's data-coverage dates: they now span an interval for which nothing at all was recorded - the gap, dated at the interval's end, moved `first_event` and `last_event`.
acceptance_criteria:
- An event asserting that data is missing does not move the account's data-coverage boundaries: a sync in which every row was refused reports no dated coverage over that interval.
- `observe()` distinguishes by kind rather than counting every dated event.
- The gap stays projection-inert everywhere else — no legs, no effect on balances, lots, income or active instruments.

title: sync_broker records the coverage gap before the assertions, in separate transactions
description:
Severity: Minor
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/sync.rs appends the ImportCoverageGap before both early returns and before fetch_portfolio; crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/sqlite.rs append_events opens one transaction per event (crates/iaam-store/src/events.rs append_event_in_order). So a gap can be committed while the portfolio fetch then fails and the call returns an error, or while an assertion append fails after earlier ones committed.

The gap itself is not false in that state - the attempt really did refuse those rows - so nothing untrue is recorded. What it leaves is a gap whose interval has no assertions from that attempt, and which the correlation rule then applies to assertions from other attempts (see the correlation bead).

The scenario has never been atomic across operations, assertions and now the gap; making it so is a store-level question about a transaction spanning a scenario, not a fix inside sync_broker. Found by an adversarial codex review of epic iaam-40vm.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Synchronise a broker interval in which some rows are refused, arranging for the portfolio fetch to fail afterwards.
2. The call returns an error, but the gap is already committed: `append_events` opens one transaction per event, and the gap is appended before both early returns and before `fetch_portfolio`.
3. The journal holds a gap whose interval carries no assertions from that attempt.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decided at the store level, not inside `sync_broker`: whether a transaction can span a scenario's operations, assertions and gap.
- If it can: a failed portfolio fetch leaves no committed gap without the assertions from the same attempt.
- If it cannot: the partial state is named, and the correlation rule is told that a gap may exist without assertions from its own attempt.

title: The out-of-interval trade suppresses every control assertion, like the quarantined row did
description:
Severity: Minor
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/sync.rs — the early return keeps its has_out_of_interval_trade half after iaam-ep05 removes the quarantine half, so a response carrying one fact dated outside [from, to] still returns assertions: 0.

It is the same conflation the epic iaam-40vm removed everywhere else: a fact whose trade date falls outside the requested interval says the gateway filtered on a different date, which is true about the interval's completeness and says nothing about the portfolio fetched independently.

It was deliberately left out of iaam-ep05 rather than folded in: an out-of-interval trade is not a refusal - the fact WAS recorded - and EventKind::ImportCoverageGap is documented as 'an import attempt refused rows', with a 'refused' count that would be zero. Deciding whether the variant should widen, or whether this needs its own fact, is a design question and not something a task passing through should settle.

Related: iaam-gawg, which asks which timestamp the T-Invest operations filter actually uses. That answer may remove the condition entirely rather than reshape it, which is a reason to wait.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sync a broker interval whose response contains a fact whose trade date falls outside the requested [from, to].
2. Observe the response reports `assertions: 0`, although the portfolio side was fetched independently of that interval.
acceptance_criteria:
- A response carrying a fact dated outside the requested [from, to] still returns the control assertions the portfolio side produced: the interval's completeness and the portfolio fetched independently are two statements, not one.
- Whether `EventKind::ImportCoverageGap` widens to cover an out-of-interval fact, or such a fact gets a record of its own, is decided explicitly. Its `refused` count must not read zero for something that was recorded.
- Wait on iaam-gawg first: knowing which timestamp the T-Invest operations filter uses may remove the condition rather than reshape it.

title: docs-debt: the broker operation-kind dictionary codes have no reference documentation
description:
Severity: Minor
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-broker/src/operation_kind.rs ChannelOperationKind::code() names buy, sell, dividend, coupon, commission, deposit, withdrawal, transfer, bond_amortisation, bond_redemption, securities_transfer_in, securities_transfer_out; grep over docs/*.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md finds none of them. An owner maps a broker source kind onto one of these codes, so the list is owner-facing surface. Pre-existing gap widened by two codes in epic iaam-zn38 (T6).

title: The channel operation-kind dictionary cannot express one owner's decision
description:
broker_operation_kinds is keyed by (broker, source_kind) with no owner column, deliberately: 'Словарь - факт о брокерском API, а не о владельце' (crates/iaam-store/migrations/0009_broker_operation_kinds.sql:11-15). set_broker_operation_kind takes no owner identifier either (crates/iaam-store/src/broker_operation_kinds.rs:116).

That is coherent for what the table calls itself. But origin = 'owner' is documented as the owner's decision, and its write path says 'the owner knows about their portfolio what the contract does not' - which is a statement about ONE portfolio. One such row applies to every owner of the installation.

So the table holds two things under one key: a fact about the broker's API, which is rightly shared, and a human's judgement about an ambiguous code, which is not. A second owner inherits the first owner's judgement with nothing marking it as someone else's.

Found while designing iaam-e00u (T6), which had to override owner-origin rows for INPUT_SECURITIES and OUTPUT_SECURITIES precisely because leaving them would have left every owner of that installation receiving fabricated cash for somebody else's override.

Decide: scope owner overrides by owner, mark the codes whose meaning the contract fixes as non-overridable, or accept the sharing and say so where an owner sets an override.
acceptance_criteria:
- One of the three is chosen and carried out: scope owner overrides by owner, mark the codes whose meaning the contract fixes as non-overridable, or accept the sharing.
- A second owner of one installation no longer silently inherits another owner's `origin = 'owner'` row — or, if sharing is accepted, that is stated where an owner sets an override.
- The table's own comment ("a fact about the broker's API, not about the owner") describes what the table actually holds.

title: A securities transfer has no fact in the journal model
description:
iaam-e00u (T6) refuses OPERATION_TYPE_INPUT_SECURITIES and OPERATION_TYPE_OUTPUT_SECURITIES rather than recording them, because the journal has nothing to record them as. The corporate-action variants are redemption, amortisation and conversion only (crates/iaam-core/src/event/corporate_action.rs:22), and a transfer between custodians is none of them.

So a real event - securities arriving from another depository, or leaving for one - is visible to the owner only as a quarantined row. The position it should have created or removed is absent, and every projection built on that position is wrong by that amount while looking complete.

Two things are needed and they belong together.

1. A fact in the journal model for a securities transfer: the instrument, the quantity, the direction, the custody on each side where known, and what happens to the lot's acquisition date and cost basis - a transfer must not reset either, or three years of ownership would be lost on moving a depository.

2. Repair of facts already recorded from these codes as cash. T6 deliberately did not repair them: deleting them without a fact to convert them into would trade one wrong number for another.

IMPORTANT about (2): the affected facts CANNOT be found from the journal alone, unlike iaam-y3a2's. The adapter keeps the operation id and discards source_kind (crates/iaam-app/src/adapters/tinkoff.rs:223,264); normalization reduces these rows to CashIn/CashOut events indistinguishable from a real deposit (crates/iaam-ingest/src/operation.rs:291); and Provenance retains source, raw hash, parser version and source_operation_id, but not the broker's operation code (crates/iaam-core/src/event/provenance.rs:51-58).

So detection must re-fetch the interval from the gateway and match on source_operation_id, or be driven by the owner. Do not plan for a predicate over stored facts - the data is not there.

Filed from T6's design, .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t6-securities-transfer-design.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria:
- The journal model carries a securities-transfer fact: instrument, quantity, direction, and the custody on each side where known.
- A transfer preserves the lot's acquisition date and cost basis. Moving a depository must not reset either.
- `OPERATION_TYPE_INPUT_SECURITIES` and `OPERATION_TYPE_OUTPUT_SECURITIES` are recorded as that fact rather than refused.
- Facts already recorded as cash from those codes are repaired by re-fetching the interval and matching `source_operation_id`, or by the owner. Not by a predicate over stored facts: the broker's operation code is not retained in provenance.

title: T-Invest custody should probably be a custodian, not a position identifier
description:
T4 (iaam-6aun) makes a trade's custody the row's position_uid, because the portfolio side of the same channel already puts positionUid into ControlClaim::PositionQuantity.custody (crates/iaam-broker/src/tinkoff/parse.rs:227-238). Without that alignment a position built from trades can never match the claim the broker raises about it.

The alignment is right and the semantics are not. position_uid identifies a position, not a place where paper is held. CustodyId elsewhere in this system means a custodian: the report channel resolves a named custodian from the directory, or a configured default (crates/iaam-ingest/src/csv_source.rs:361-377), and the reference data lists custody places (crates/iaam-store/src/reference.rs:207).

So this channel currently uses one field name for two different meanings depending on which channel filled it, and a report and an API sync of the same holding would disagree about custody while both being right by their own rule.

The conflation predates T4 - the portfolio side made it - and T4 deliberately did not resolve it, because deciding the channel's custody model inside a task about trades is how the monolithic design failed three reviews.

Decide: map a real custodian for this channel, keep position_uid and rename what CustodyId means for API-sourced facts, or accept the divergence and document it where a reader of a position will see it.
acceptance_criteria:
- One of the three is chosen and carried out: map a real custodian for this channel, keep `position_uid` and say what `CustodyId` means for API-sourced facts, or accept the divergence.
- A position built from trades and the claim the broker raises about it agree on custody by one rule, not by two rules that happen to coincide.
- Whatever is decided is written where a reader of a position will see it, not only in this bead.

title: Establish whether the T-Invest commission is per unit or per turnover
description:
T3 allocates an order's commission across its fills by quantity (design 3, .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t3-trade-money-design.md), matching the convention already in the code: crates/iaam-core/src/projection/lots.rs:381 allocates an actual payment to lots in proportion to quantity.

The alternative reading is that a brokerage commission is a percentage of turnover, which would weight by quantity x price. The contract does not say (operations.proto:501, MoneyValue commission = 43, no basis given), and the two weights agree whenever every fill of an order shares one price - which every fill in the recorded response does. So nothing available distinguishes them, and the choice was made on local consistency rather than on evidence.

The error is confined to the split between lots of one order; the order total is preserved either way. It shows up as a wrong cost basis per lot, and therefore a wrong gain on a partial sale.

Needs a live multi-fill order whose fills executed at different prices, with the commission reported. Then compare both weightings against the reported figure.
acceptance_criteria:
- A live multi-fill order whose fills executed at different prices, with the commission reported, is obtained. Until then nothing here can be settled: the two weightings agree on every response in the repository.
- Both weightings — by quantity, and by quantity x price — are compared against the reported figure.
- The allocation rule is stated with the evidence that chose it. If the evidence cannot be obtained, that is recorded and the quantity weighting is kept deliberately rather than by default.

title: Establish the trading day's timezone for T-Invest fills
description:
T2 derives a fill's trade date and source time in UTC (design 9, .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t2-trade-becomes-fact-design.md), because that is how the channel is already read: source_time_or_reject converts to UTC (crates/iaam-broker/src/tinkoff/parse.rs:563) and the order date takes .date() of the parsed RFC 3339 value (parse.rs:549-551).

The failure mode is a fill executed between 00:00 and 03:00 Moscow time: it lands on the previous UTC day, and T-Bank runs sessions in that window for some instruments. A trade dated a day early is not a rounding difference - it moves the fact into another reporting period and can change lot matching order.

What is missing is evidence, not an opinion: no response in the repository contains a night-session fill. Choosing Europe/Moscow now would be inventing a rule rather than reading one, and it would also mean reading the trade date and the order date of one response in two different zones, plus a timezone database this workspace does not depend on.

Needs a live response containing a fill executed between 00:00 and 03:00 MSK. Then decide the zone for the whole channel - both dates - and state it once.
acceptance_criteria:
- A live response containing a fill executed between 00:00 and 03:00 MSK is obtained. Choosing a zone without one would be inventing a rule rather than reading one.
- The zone is decided for the whole channel — trade date and order date both — and applied in one place, not two.
- If a timezone database becomes a dependency, that is a deliberate addition and is stated.

title: Two identical fills of one order reach the owner as PossibleDuplicate
description:
The operation fingerprint covers {v, account, kind, dates} only (crates/iaam-ingest/src/dedup.rs:350-355). source_time is deliberately excluded, because a source can name a calendar date without asserting a moment.

For a trade that exclusion costs something. After iaam-dz94 (T2) one order expands into one fact per fill, and two fills equal in quantity, price and day share a fingerprint. dedup::assess finds no key match - {op}#{num} differs per fill - then finds the fingerprint among known records from a different document; the API channel has document: None and same_document is false whenever either side is absent (dedup.rs:243-248). sync_broker pushes each recorded event onto known inside the loop (crates/iaam-app/src/scenarios/sync.rs:126), so the second fill is compared against the first.

Result: both facts are recorded - the append happens before the verdict is chosen (sync.rs:113-122) - but the owner sees PossibleDuplicate on every order with two identical fills, which is an ordinary market event. Nothing is lost; the signal is diluted.

The obvious fix is to include source_time in the canonical form, and it is not obviously right: CANONICAL_VERSION would change, every stored fingerprint would stop matching, and every re-import of every source would look fresh. That cost belongs to a task that can weigh it across all channels, which is why T2 accepted the noise instead (design 8, .internal/specs/2026-08-31-t2-trade-becomes-fact-design.md).

Decide: live with it, narrow same_document for API channels, or version the canonical form.
acceptance_criteria:
- One of the three is chosen: live with the noise, narrow `same_document` for API channels, or version the canonical form.
- If the canonical form is versioned, the cost is planned across all channels first: every stored fingerprint stops matching and every re-import of every source looks fresh.
- Two identical fills of one order no longer reach the owner as `PossibleDuplicate` — or, if the noise is accepted, the verdict's explanation says why an ordinary market event looks like this.

title: Заслон на висячие $ref в OpenAPI-документе
description:
Severity: Minor
Confidence: Confirmed
Evidence: crates/iaam-server/tests/contract.rs не проверяет разрешимость ссылок; при мерже feat/iaam-d8b.13-posting-reconciliation OfferExerciseDto был снят из components(schemas(...)) в openapi.rs — сейчас безопасно (utoipa 5 добирает его через JournalFactDto), но заслона нет. Разовая проба обходом всех $ref прошла.
acceptance_criteria:
- A contract test walks every `$ref` in the generated OpenAPI document and fails on one that resolves to nothing.
- The guard is proven by removing a schema from `components(schemas(...))` that nothing else pulls in, and observing the test fail.

title: Уровень дедупликации вычисляется, но владельцу не показывается
description:
DedupLevel и DedupLevel::number() не используются нигде за пределами crates/iaam-ingest и тестов: grep по crates/iaam-app и crates/iaam-server не находит ни одного упоминания.

При этом doc-комментарий модуля называет номер уровня частью объяснения решения владельцу, а §10.6 задаёт нумерацию уровней. Решение PossibleDuplicate доходит до владельца без указания, КАКОЙ уровень дедупликации сработал — то есть без того самого объяснения.

Обнаружено при исполнении iaam-pb3a: мутанты в DedupLevel::number выживали в том числе потому, что значение никуда не течёт, и убить их поведенческим тестом невозможно — тест вынужденно закрепляет константу.

Либо уровень должен доходить до ответа API, либо number() — мёртвый публичный код и его следует убрать. Решение за владельцем.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Решено: уровень показывается владельцу либо number() удаляется.
- Если показывается — значение называет себя в API и покрыто нетавтологичным тестом.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn DedupLevel crates/iaam-app crates/iaam-server` — no hits: the value never leaves `iaam-ingest`.
2. Import a batch that yields `PossibleDuplicate` and read the API response: it names no deduplication level, though §10.6 numbers the levels and the module doc calls the number part of the explanation owed to the owner.

title: E3.4: разбор изменений между снимками графика (ScheduleDiff, §2.2)
description:
Спека §2.2 объявляет ScheduleDiff = Added | Removed | Moved | Amended | Ambiguous для объяснимости: назвать поимённо, что изменилось между снимками. Расчёт от него не зависит — снимок берётся целиком. Потребителя нет, пока нет отчёта об изменениях графика или экрана аудита.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Разница между двумя снимками названа поимённо, а не числом изменившихся строк.
- Сдвиг даты возврата номинала, неотличимый от объявления нового, помечается Ambiguous и расчёт не блокирует.
notes: Перенесено под E8 · Веб-UI (2026-08-28): ScheduleDiff чисто вычислим, но по §2.2 существует ради объяснимости, а потребитель у него один — отчёт об изменениях графика или экран аудита. Строить его до потребителя значит замораживать форму разницы под воображаемый экран.

title: Планировщик синхронизации с брокером
description: Отложено из E2. Сейчас синхронизация запускается маршрутом руками. Нужен планировщик с окном, ограничением частоты и внятным поведением при отказе брокера: частичная выгрузка не должна выдаваться за полную.
acceptance_criteria:
- Synchronisation runs on a schedule with a window and a rate limit, not only from a route driven by hand.
- A broker failure yields a partial export that is reported as partial. A partial export is never presented as a complete one.
- The manual route keeps working alongside the scheduler.

title: Справка налогового агента как источник подтверждений
description: Отложено из E2. Справка 2-НДФЛ/налогового агента подтверждает удержанный налог и дивиденды; понадобится эпику налогов (E5), но как источник сверки заводится отдельно.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tax-agent statement is parsed as a confirmation source for withheld tax and for dividends.
- It stands as a reconciliation source in its own right, independent of E5's tax calculation, and is filed so that E5 can use it without owning it.

title: Депозитарный отчёт как источник подтверждений
description: Отложено из E2. Депозитарий подтверждает количества бумаг независимо от брокера — это ещё одно основание независимости (§10.3). Нужен парсер формата и канал.
acceptance_criteria:
- A parser for the depositary report format, and a channel that feeds it into the journal.
- Quantities are confirmed independently of the broker, giving §10.3 independence a second ground rather than a second reading of the same one.

title: Один мьютекс на всё хранилище сериализует чтения и записи
description: На одного пользователя это не проблема. При появлении второго писателя понадобится пул соединений и разделение читателей и писателей.
acceptance_criteria:
- A second writer is possible: readers and writers no longer contend on one mutex over the whole store.
- The change is measured, not asserted: a test or benchmark shows concurrent reads proceeding during a write.
- Until a second writer exists this stays deferred; single-user correctness is not affected.

title: iaam-cli: локальные команды поверх iaam-app
description:
Filed before `iaam-bootstrap` existed. That crate now ships the `iaam` binary
with `serve`, `claim`, `token` and `broker` — administration of the instance and
its credentials. So a CLI over the application layer exists; what this bead
asked for beyond administration was never written down.

What is undefined and has to be decided before this can be worked: which
non-administrative operations belong at the console at all. The founding design
puts the owner's day-to-day work behind the agent and the HTTP API, and the
import skills run against files the agent never holds — so a second, local
surface for reports or import needs its own justification rather than being
assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either a named list of console operations that must exist outside the API,
  each with the reason it cannot live behind the agent, and those implemented;
- or this bead is closed as superseded by `iaam-bootstrap`, recording that
  decision.
